data.description:
# Move proxy startup and management out of user space (systemd system service)

## Background — full diagnosis (forensic analysis, 2026-07-31)

The LLM proxy repeatedly dies during/after agent test runs. Root-cause analysis of the system journal, proxy log, herdr logs, pi-agent session files, and systemd state shows:

**Mechanism (proven):** The proxy (started via `nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh` inside a login session) is killed when the ENTIRE user systemd slice (`user-1000.slice`) is torn down — the user manager (`systemd --user`) goes to `exit.target`, which SIGTERMs every process in the slice. The proxy log confirms a clean SIGTERM-driven graceful shutdown (e.g. `2026-07-31 17:19:32,602 - Shutting down LLama Proxy Server`). `nohup` only ignores SIGHUP; it provides zero protection against systemd slice teardown.

**Recurring signature (same second, all events):** wireplumber `stopped by signal: Terminated` + `sshd: session closed for user rgardler` + `sudo: session closed` + `systemd --user: Activating special unit exit.target`. Fired at 12:16:21, 12:32:48, 13:48:32, 13:56:39 and 17:19:32 on 2026-07-31; the proxy died at 12:41:02, 13:57:25 and 17:19:32 as the containing session scope (`session-1568/1584/1615.scope`) was deactivated.

**Not normal logout:** On 2026-07-31 18:04:43 an SSH session closed and NOTHING died — that session is still in `closing` state (systemd-logind `KillUserProcesses=no`); the proxy and pi agent are still running inside it. So a plain SSH logout does NOT kill the proxy — confirming operator experience.

**Tests are not the direct killer (evidence):** the audit Phase 2 model's last recorded action was running the gated test suite (`pytest proxy/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider`; live/process-killing tests self-skip). A comprehensive grep of all test files found zero process-killing patterns; tests that previously caused "SSH session ejection and server shutdown" were removed (commit 0e1a2f5) or gated behind opt-in env vars (commit c83921e). No kill command was found in operator bash history, herdr logs, cron (sysstat/hourly), cleanup-all.sh, or the ship skill. The teardowns correlate with SSH session closes (all from laptop 192.168.0.191); test runs merely happen inside those sessions.

**Root cause:** the proxy's lifecycle is coupled to the operator's interactive login session. Any session teardown (drop or logout) can cascade into a full user-slice teardown (user manager exit), killing the proxy. The existing user-scoped systemd unit (`~/.config/systemd/user/llama-proxy.service`) does not help: it is enabled and auto-starts on login but fails with `status=216/GROUP` ("Failed to determine supplementary groups: Operation not permitted") in this environment, and being a user service it would still live inside the user slice.

## Proposed fix — run the proxy as a systemd SYSTEM service (outside user space)

Move startup and management of the proxy (and therefore its llama-server and TTS children) out of the user session entirely, into a root-managed system unit under `system.slice`.

1. **Create/install `/etc/systemd/system/llama-proxy.service`** (system unit, managed by PID 1), based on the system-service variant already documented in `docs/systemd/llama-proxy.service`:
   - `User=rgardler`, `Group=rgardler` (so it can read `config.yaml`, `~/.pi/agent/auth.json`, GPU/podman resources); if the "supplementary groups" failure reproduces under PID 1, drop `Group=` (known workaround).
   - `ExecStart=/home/rgardler/projects/llm/proxy/.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn proxy.server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` with `LLAMA_PROXY_CONFIG` / `LLAMA_START_SCRIPT` env.
   - `Restart=always`, `RestartSec=5`; `WantedBy=multi-user.target` (auto-start on boot); log to `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (already exists, chown rgardler).
   - Runs in `system.slice` — outside `user-1000.slice`, so SSH session close/teardown can never reach it.
2. **Disable/remove the user unit** `~/.config/systemd/user/llama-proxy.service` (currently enabled; auto-start at login fails with 216/GROUP and conflicts).
3. **Keep llama-server + TTS as proxy children** (start-llama.sh / start-qwentts.sh) — they inherit the system service scope, staying outside user space. Port-based zombie cleanup from LP-0MS4R1E0F005CE8V already handles stale TTS processes.
4. **Update `start-proxy.sh --restart`** to manage the system service (`systemctl restart llama-proxy` after stopping any dev/nohup instance) or document the service as the canonical path; keep the nohup path for development only.
5. **Update docs**: `docs/systemd/llama-proxy.service` (make system service the recommended variant for this environment), `proxy/README.md` lifecycle section.
6. **Acceptance/integration tests**: add a test script/check that verifies the service survives a real SSH logout/login cycle and that `/health` stays healthy with an unchanged proxy PID; verify auto-start after reboot.

## User Stories

- As an operator, I want the proxy managed by a root systemd service outside my login session, so that SSH disconnects, logouts and agent test runs can never take down the LLM API.
- As an operator, I want the service to auto-start on boot and self-restart on crash, so the proxy is always available without manual intervention.
- As a developer, I want `start-proxy.sh` and the docs to reflect the system-service deployment model, so there is a single canonical startup path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The proxy runs as a systemd system service in `system.slice` (verified via `systemctl status` and cgroup), not inside any `session-NNNN.scope`.
2. A real SSH logout/login cycle (or dropped connection) does NOT terminate the proxy: `/health` remains healthy and the proxy PID is unchanged after reconnect.
3. The service starts automatically on boot (`WantedBy=multi-user.target`).
4. A `kill -9` on the proxy is recovered by `Restart=always` (new PID, healthy /health).
5. TTS and llama-server remain functional as children of the proxy service; TTS zombie/port cleanup (LP-0MS4R1E0F005CE8V) still works across restarts.
6. The failing user unit is disabled/removed; no `status=216/GROUP` failures on login.

Verify podman/GPU access works from the system service context; if rootless podman needs the user session, use `User=rgardler` with `systemctl --user` alternatives or a rootful podman setup.

- **Scope:** strictly the proxy deployment/management move; no changes to proxy routing/model logic.

# Intake Brief: Occasional "Error: Provider finish_reason: error" from remote streaming

## Problem statement

Pi sessions intermittently fail with the hard error `Error: Provider finish_reason: error` after the proxy's Tier-1 upstream-retry chain exhausts mid-stream. The trigger is a 30s per-chunk idle timeout misfiring on slow-but-alive reasoning-model upstreams (opencode-go / deepseek-v4-flash on large contexts), followed by expensive whole-request retries that also stall, and finally a synthetic `finish_reason: error` that the client surfaces as a fatal error — with **no fallback to the next provider** because the streaming response was already committed to the client.

## Users

Pi operators using remote providers (opencode-go deepseek-v4-flash and similar slow reasoning upstreams) on large-context sessions.

- As a user, I want a slow upstream that pauses >30s while reasoning to not be treated as dead, so my long-running request completes instead of erroring after ~8 minutes.
- As a user, I want a genuinely failing upstream to fail fast rather than re-sending a huge request three more times, so I can retry quickly instead of waiting minutes.
- As a user, I do not want to see `Error: Provider finish_reason: error` for transient upstream stalls.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Raising `server.upstream_idle_timeout_seconds` (default 30 → 120) no longer misfires stall detection on upstreams that pause between chunks during long reasoning on large prompts; a test simulates a chunk gap of 60–90s and asserts the stream is NOT killed/retried.
- [ ] When a remote stream stalls after at least one content-bearing chunk has been delivered, the proxy does NOT restart the whole request from scratch; it terminates the stream immediately (no retry) so the client can retry with full context.
- [ ] Retries (Tier 1) only occur while zero content has been delivered; the retry count/backoff behavior for the zero-content case is unchanged (bounded exponential backoff, max attempts, then `finish_reason: error`).
- [ ] A stall on a large-context request (e.g. 30K+ tokens) completes or fails within a bounded time — no longer up to ~8 minutes of wasted retries on a multi-hundred-KB prompt.
- [ ] All existing tests pass, plus new unit tests covering: (a) idle-timeout tuning behavior, (b) no-retry-after-content policy, (c) retry-before-content still works, (d) config defaults.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from the above — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Do not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- The per-chunk idle timeout must remain shorter than the httpx `remote_http_client.read_timeout_seconds` (300s) so stall detection fires before `ReadTimeout`.
- Retry-after-content removal must not regress the existing "Remote ReadTimeout bounded-timeout" behavior (LP-0MRDI0FYQ008BI5Y) for streams that produced no content.
- The `finish_reason: error` event contract with the fallback chain in `provider.py` (Tier 2 cooldown / Tier 3 circuit breaker) must be preserved.
- Client-side auto-recovery is out of scope for this project — tracked separately in SorraAgents (SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW).
- Transparent mid-stream fallback to the next provider (option C) is explicitly a LARGER follow-up, not part of this item.

## Existing state

- `server.upstream_idle_timeout_seconds: 30` (proxy/config.yaml) — reduced from 60s for "faster stall detection" (LP-0MRFEXXVC001RYKB).
- Local path uses `stream_idle_timeout_seconds: 120` for Qwen3 reasoning pauses (LP-0MS14PM7J003XPS8) — the remote path is inconsistent with this.
- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py:_handle_remote_streaming` retries the whole request (max `upstream_retry_max_attempts: 3`, backoff 2/4/8s cap 60s) on stall even after content has been delivered; on exhaustion yields `{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "error"}`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py:_handle_streaming_success` returns any 2xx `StreamingResponse` immediately — no mid-stream fallback possible.
- Observed incident 2026-07-31 21:36–21:44: 35K-token prompt → stall at 21:37:58, retries 21:41:41 (attempt 3), exhausted 21:44:40 → `Stream finished: reason=error` → client error.

## Desired change

1. **Config:** raise `server.upstream_idle_timeout_seconds` in `proxy/config.yaml` from 30 → 120 (matching the local `stream_idle_timeout_seconds: 120` reasoning-model timeout). Update the config comment documenting why.
2. **Code default:** raise the code-level fallback default in `_handle_remote_streaming` from 60 → 120 (used when the config key is absent — currently `60` in both the function parameter resolution and the local default). Keep both in sync with the config value.
3. **Code (`_handle_remote_streaming`):** track whether any content-bearing chunk was delivered before the stall (`_has_content`, already computed via `_delta_has_content`); if content was delivered, do not retry — terminate the stream immediately (synthetic `finish_reason: error`) so the client sees a clear terminal state quickly. Only retry when zero content was delivered (guard the stall `_should_retry = True` path with `not _has_content`).

## Risks & assumptions

- Raising `upstream_idle_timeout_seconds` to 120 delays detection of a genuinely dead upstream by up to 90s vs today (accepted by user, Q2). Mitigation: read timeout cap (300s) still bounds total wait; circuit breaker still records stalls.
- No-retry-after-content makes partial responses end abruptly at the client; the user must retry manually. Mitigation: the client-side auto-recovery work item (SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW) addresses recovery; keep the synthetic `finish_reason: error` so pi classifies it consistently.
- Content-detection edge cases (tool-call-only / reasoning-only streams) must not be misclassified as "no content". Mitigation: reuse `_delta_has_content` semantics from LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL.
- Assumption: the 30s gaps observed on large prompts are slow generation (reasoning/prefill), not dead connections; if the upstream were truly dead, raising the timeout only delays detection, so the no-retry-after-content policy keeps failure time bounded.
- Scope-creep guard: transparent mid-stream fallback (option C) is deliberately a follow-up item, not part of this work item; client-side changes live in SorraAgents (SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/config.yaml` — raise `upstream_idle_timeout_seconds` to 120, update comments.
- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — `_handle_remote_streaming`: content-aware retry policy (no retry after content delivered).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — only if retry-policy constants/defaults need centralization (likely minimal/no change).
- `proxy/tests/` — new tests: stall-gap tolerance, no-retry-after-content, retry-before-content preserved, config defaults. Existing: `tests/test_upstream_stall_detection.py`, `tests/test_stream_finish_reason_on_error.py`, `tests/test_remote_empty_response_retry.py`, `tests/test_stall_circuit_breaker_integration.py` are directly relevant.

## Related work

- **LP-0MRE4WPX30064XPU** (completed) — "Implement retry logic for remote provider ReadTimeout during streaming". Established Tier-1 retries and the `finish_reason: error` contract.
- **LP-0MRDI0FYQ008BI5Y** (completed) — "Remote ReadTimeout bounded-timeout verification tests". Must not regress.
- **LP-0MRFFZVHB005XWPF** (completed) — "Wire circuit breaker into retry-exhausted path". Tier-3 circuit breaker records stalls at exhaustion.
- **LP-0MRFEXXVC001RYKB** (completed, referenced in config) — stall circuit breaker + the 60→30s idle-timeout reduction.
- **LP-0MS14PM7J003XPS8** (referenced in config) — local `stream_idle_timeout_seconds` raised to 120 for reasoning pauses (the precedent for this change).
- **LP-0MRB29HJ1009OR6G** (completed) — "SSE Streaming Generator Hangs on Missing [DONE]".
- **LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL** (completed) — "deepseek-v4 tool calls fail: proxy misclassifies tool-call-only streams as empty responses" (content detection semantics).
- **SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW** (SorraAgents, in-progress) — client-side (pi) auto-recovery from `Provider finish_reason: error`. `discovered-from` this item.
- Pi client behavior: `pi-ai/dist/api/openai-completions.js` `mapStopReason()` maps unknown/error finish_reason → `{stopReason:"error", errorMessage:"Provider finish_reason: <reason>"}` and throws.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MQMC3S6Q007AC5G** – Container strategy & Containerfile finalization (completed)
- **LP-0MRMGUEVR0002S5W** – Fix local_active_queries leak in streaming error paths causing all requests to skip Qwen3 (completed)
- **LP-0MQ3WE2ZG003R556** – When no slots are available make retry1155 minutes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MQSFWFB1007R2I7-extract-level-from-score/docs/ralph.md` — matched: error, fix, high, occasional, opencode, priority, provider, rca, reason, remote, running, session, sessions, still, streaming, user
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MQSFWFB1007R2I7-extract-level-from-score/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: deepseek, error, fix, flash, high, intent, opencode, priority, provider, reason, remote, running, session, still, user
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MQSFWFB1007R2I7-extract-level-from-score/skill/ralph/scripts/ralph_loop.py` — matched: error, finish, fix, high, intent, opencode, rca, reason, remote, running, session, sessions, still, streaming, user

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Fix scope: Are you OK with A+B (config + retry-policy code change) as the target, with C (transparent mid-stream fallback) as a larger follow-up?" — Answer (user): "1 LGTM". Source: interactive reply. Accepted: scope = A (raise idle timeout) + B (no retry after content); C deferred to a follow-up work item.
- Q: "Trade-off: Accepting a higher idle timeout means a genuinely-dead upstream takes 90–120s to detect (vs 30s today). Acceptable?" — Answer (user): "2 LGTM". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Client side: Is changing pi's client behavior out of scope (proxy-side fix only)?" — Answer (user): "3 Create a work item in ../SorraAgents and run wl sync when done". Source: interactive reply. Result: created SA-0MS9GFH5H0033TQW in /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents; `wl sync` run at intake completion.

## Summary

The proxy's GPU-wedge self-healer (introduced in LP-0MS91DHQ9003EGB0) is false-positiving on the Strix Halo APU, causing constant model unload/reload churn that severely degrades agent performance.

## Problem

The wedge detector fires when `gpu_busy_percent >= 90` AND all slots are idle for 2 consecutive health checks (interval 10s), then unloads and reloads the Qwen3 model.

On this AMD Strix Halo APU (Radeon 8060S iGPU, gfx1151), `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_busy_percent` is **pinned at 100% regardless of actual GPU state**: 30/30 samples over 30s read 100 while power draw showed the GPU idle (54W idle vs 115W when genuinely computing). The busy counter cannot discriminate real work from idle on this hardware.

## Impact (measured 2026-07-31)

- **144 wedge-triggered model unloads in one day** (144 unload / 288 reload log events)
- Worst stretch 21:07-21:29: unload→reload loop every ~40s — the model was never stably loaded
- Each unload kills in-flight local requests (13 stream errors: RemoteProtocolError x9, StreamConsumed x3, NameError x1) and forces a 30-60s reload of the 23 GB model
- Killed requests fall back to remote providers, compounding latency
- The model is currently only stable because agents keep slots busy; any >=20s idle moment re-triggers the loop

## User stories

- As an operator I want the wedge detector to stop unloading the model during normal idle periods so local inference is always available.
- As an operator I still want protection against genuinely wedged GPUs (hung KV-cache slot save/restore, LP-0MS91D782006XIR6) so the stack can self-heal.

## Suggested approach

- Add a discriminating signal that separates real wedges from counter artifacts on this APU. Candidates: power draw threshold (real wedge observed at ~53W with NO compute; genuine compute runs 110-115W — not sufficient alone since idle also reads low power), requiring `is_processing=True` with no token progress for N seconds, or sampling the counter over a window rather than a single read.
- Alternatively disable via config `llama_gpu_wedge_detection_enabled: false` as an interim mitigation while a reliable detector is designed.
- Consider excluding embeddings instances and non-APU-incompatible probes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the fix deployed, the proxy does NOT unload/reload Qwen3 during sustained idle periods (no wedge detections over a 30+ min idle window with agents stopped).
- [ ] Genuine wedge conditions (if reproducible) still trigger recovery, or a documented decision is recorded to disable the feature for this hardware class.
- [ ] In-flight requests are not killed by spurious unloads (stream error count drops to ~0 over a 24h window).
- [ ] Unit tests cover the detection logic with a pinned-at-100% busy counter input.
- [ ] Unload/reload event count drops from 144/day to near zero on a 24h observation.

## Related

- discovered-from: proxy analysis 2026-07-31 (agent session)
- related-to: LP-0MS91DHQ9003EGB0 (self-healing addition), LP-0MS91D782006XIR6 (original real wedge), LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO (slot save/restore timeouts)
- blocked-by: none

## Summary

Move per-chunk SSE logging (the `STREAM CHUNK | data: ...` lines) behind a `--verbose` flag so normal operation stops writing millions of lines per day.

## Problem / Context

- `log_response_chunk` (proxy/router_helpers.py:204) logs every streamed SSE chunk at INFO level via `srv.logger.info("STREAM CHUNK | ...")`.
- Measured impact 2026-07-31: proxy.log reached **920 MB in ~6h**, ~**10k lines/min**, 6.6M lines/day. The uvicorn proxy process burned ~16-18% CPU, partly on log I/O.
- There is already a console-suppression handler (proxy/session.py) so chunk content is excluded from console, but it is still written to the file handler at INFO.
- No `--verbose` flag exists yet on the proxy CLI.

## User stories

- As an operator I want normal proxy operation to log only significant events so log volume and proxy CPU drop.
- As a developer I want to re-enable per-chunk SSE logging on demand (e.g., `--verbose`) for debugging stream issues.

## Suggested approach

- Add a `--verbose` CLI flag (and/or config key, e.g. `logging.verbose_chunks`) that gates `log_response_chunk` to DEBUG level by default; when verbose is set, log at INFO (or keep a separate DEBUG logger).
- Ensure session.py console-suppression behavior remains consistent.
- Confirm no test asserts on STREAM CHUNK INFO output that would break; adjust tests to the new level.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Default startup: `STREAM CHUNK` lines are NOT written to proxy.log (log growth drops by >99% over a 24h window; e.g., from ~920MB/6h to well under 100MB/24h).
- [ ] Starting the proxy with `--verbose` restores per-chunk logging.
- [ ] Existing tests pass; any test that depends on chunk-level logging is updated to use verbose mode.
- [ ] Documentation (README/HOST_INSTALL) mentions the flag.

## Related

- discovered-from: proxy analysis 2026-07-31 (agent session)

## Summary

After the GPU-wedge false-positive fix (LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP) is deployed, verify that slot save/restore and the session-cache ratio actually work end-to-end. Slot saves have been failing with ReadTimeouts and `cached_ratio=0.00` appears on every routing check, meaning local requests are treated as cold full-prefill every turn.

## Problem / Context

Measured 2026-07-31 (proxy + llama-server logs):
- `slot_save failed slot=N error=ReadTimeout` warnings (slot snapshot files are 600MB-1.3GB each; 27 GB of slot-cache files currently on disk).
- `cached_ratio=0.00` on every `routing_check` line — `update_cached_ratio` (proxy/provider.py) never gets a non-zero cached_tokens.
- Slots do show internal LCP reuse (`selected slot by LCP similarity, sim_best = 0.982`) but the proxy-level session cache credit is not reflected.
- Suspected interactions: GPU wedge/reload churn invalidating caches, slot-save timeouts wedging the GPU (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO), and save timeouts preventing ratio updates.

## User stories

- As an operator I want slot snapshots to save and restore reliably so multi-turn agent sessions resume without a full prefill every turn.
- As an operator I want the `cached_ratio` in routing logs to reflect real cache hits (non-zero) so routing decisions use cache state correctly.

## Suggested approach

- After the wedge fix is live: restart the stack cleanly, run a multi-turn local session, then check:
  1. `slot_save` warnings disappear from proxy.log.
  2. `cached_ratio` becomes non-zero in `routing_check` lines for a continuing session.
  3. Second turn latency drops vs first turn (cache hit benefit measurable).
  4. No ReadTimeout errors on slot save/restore in llama-server.log.
- If saves still time out, scope a follow-up fix (e.g., reduce checkpoint frequency/size, raise save timeout, exclude huge contexts >50k from snapshotting).
- Consider a canary test or monitoring check that fails when cached_ratio stays 0 across a session.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After fix deployment and a clean restart, a 5+ turn local session produces ZERO `slot_save failed` warnings.
- [ ] `routing_check` logs for that session show `cached_ratio` > 0 on turn 2+.
- [ ] Turn 2+ latency is measurably lower than turn 1 (documented numbers in a comment on this item).
- [ ] Any remaining save timeouts are triaged into a follow-up work item with evidence.

## Related

- blocked-by: LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP (GPU-wedge false-positive fix)
- related-to: LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO (slot save/restore timeouts wedge GPU), LP-0MS91D782006XIR6 (original wedge)

## Summary

Adjust the llama-server parallelism so the local Qwen3 model runs 3 slots during daytime (agent concurrency is low, context size matters more) and 6 slots at night (batch workloads / agents run unattended and benefit from higher parallelism).

## Problem / Context

- Parallelism is controlled via the `LLAMA_PARALLEL` env var in `start-llama.sh` (currently default 1; both running instances use `--parallel 4` hardcoded in their cmdline).
- The dedicated Qwen3 instance (port 57527) and router (port 8080) both run `--parallel 4`.
- Changing slots requires a llama-server restart; a time-based mechanism must switch 3↔6 at the configured boundaries with minimal disruption.
- Day = 3 slots (fewer concurrent large-context requests thrashing the iGPU; each slot gets more GPU time), Night = 6 slots (unattended batch work benefits from more concurrency).
- Observed context: 4 parallel slots x 15-30k token contexts currently thrash the 40-CU iGPU (generation collapsed to 1.4-7.8 tok/s under contention).

## User stories

- As an operator I want the local model to use 3 slots during the day so interactive agent turns are not slowed by GPU contention.
- As an operator I want 6 slots at night so unattended batch agent runs get more concurrency.
- As an operator I want the switch to be automatic and to take effect without manual restarts.

## Suggested approach

- A scheduler that toggles `LLAMA_PARALLEL` and restarts the llama-server instances at the day/night boundary (e.g., cron entry or systemd timer invoking a wrapper that writes the new parallel value and restarts the services).
- Boundaries to confirm with operator (e.g., day 08:00-22:00 = 3, night 22:00-08:00 = 6).
- Ensure slot-cache / session continuity across the restart (slot snapshots are on disk under /home/rgardler/projects/llm/slot-cache).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /slots` on the Qwen3 instance reports 3 slots during day window and 6 during night window.
- [ ] The switch happens automatically at the configured boundary without manual intervention.
- [ ] The restart at switch time does not lose session state (slot snapshots restored; no orphaned leases).
- [ ] Documentation updated in README/HOST_INSTALL describing the mechanism and how to change boundaries/slot counts.
- [ ] Tests cover the boundary logic (time-window selection) and the restart trigger.

- related-to: start-llama.sh (LLAMA_PARALLEL), scripts/systemd (service definitions)

## Summary

During full-suite proxy test runs (`pytest tests/`), the running production
proxy (llama-server + TTS + proxy on ports 8000/8080/8081) goes down. A
full-suite run on 2026-07-31 killed the proxy mid-run (observed twice). We
need to identify the specific test(s) responsible.

## Problem

The full proxy test suite spawns processes, uses ports, and may kill
processes by name/pattern. One or more tests interfere with the live proxy:
either killing its processes, stealing its ports, or exhausting resources
(GPU/RAM - the 23GB Qwen3 model is loaded).

## Approach (operator-approved)

Run the full test suite one test at a time (`pytest <nodeid>` per
invocation), logging START/END of each test, then verifying the proxy is
still up via `GET http://localhost:8000/health` after each test. The first
test after which the health check fails is the culprit.

## User stories

- As an operator I want to know exactly which test kills the proxy so the
  test can be made safe (env guard, port isolation, process-scoped kill).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A diagnostic log records start/end/exit of every test in the suite
- [ ] The proxy health status is checked after every test and recorded
- [ ] The culprit test(s) are identified by node id
- [ ] The proxy is restored (restarted) at the end of the diagnostic

## Related

- discovered-from: proxy analysis 2026-07-31 (full-suite run killed proxy twice)
- related-to: LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP (GPU-wedge false positives; full-suite run aborted the implementation session)

## Problem

`start-proxy.sh --restart` uses `pkill -f 'tts-server'` and `pkill -f 'qwentts'` to clean up TTS processes. `pkill -f` matches ANY process whose full command line contains the substring — not just actual TTS processes. AI-agent subprocesses (e.g. pi audit/implement model calls) pass prompts containing 'tts-server' and 'qwentts' as argv, so they are SIGTERM/SIGKILLed on every proxy restart.

## Impact (observed)

During the audit of LP-0MS4R1E0F005CE8V, the audit runner's pi subprocess was killed twice by `start-proxy.sh --restart` (run by a concurrent session), each time aborting the audit mid-run with an empty log. Any agent or user process with 'tts-server'/'qwentts' in its argv is vulnerable.

discovered-from:LP-0MS4R1E0F005CE8V

## Suggested fix

Scope the kill to actual TTS process trees instead of substring argv matching:
- Prefer port-based detection (fuser/ss on the TTS port) over pkill, consistent with the AC1 cleanup in lifecycle.py (`_kill_process_on_port`).
- Or match the exact binary path / process name (`pkill -x tts-server` or full-path pattern) and the wrapper script by its full path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `start-proxy.sh --restart` no longer kills processes whose argv merely contains 'tts-server' or 'qwentts' (e.g. an agent subprocess running a TTS-related prompt).
2. All genuine TTS processes (start-qwentts.sh wrapper and tts-server binary) are still reliably killed on --restart.
3. Existing restart test coverage (tests/test_start_proxy_restart*.sh) still passes.
4. Documentation updated if behavior changes.

## Summary (RCA complete — LP-0MS9H56R9000RIYF investigation)

The full proxy test suite (single pytest process) kills the running proxy
stack every time, at ~89-93% (test_switching_sse.py / test_stream_finish_reason_on_error.py region). Root cause confirmed by strace:

**`python -m pytest` calls `kill(-1, SIGTERM)`** — a system-wide SIGTERM that
takes down the whole proxy stack (proxy, llama-server, TTS, children) with
no proxy-internal trigger.

### Mechanism
1. `test_switching_sse.py::test_ensure_model_loaded_emits_switching_then_ready`
   calls `server.ensure_model_loaded("new-model")` and mocks
   `start_llama_server` but **NOT `stop_llama_server`**.
2. `ensure_model_loaded` (lifecycle.py, non-router path) calls the real
   `srv.stop_llama_server()`.
3. In the full-suite pytest process, `server.llama_process` is a
   `MagicMock(poll=lambda: None, pid=1)` (set by the autouse fixture in
   `test_stream_finish_reason_on_error.py` / similar tests, left in module
   state).
4. `stop_llama_server()` → `_kill_process_group(mock)` → `os.killpg(pid=1,
   SIGTERM)`.
5. **Python's `os.killpg(pgid, sig)` NEGATES the pgid**: `os.killpg(1, ...)`
   issues the syscall `kill(-1, ...)` = send signal to EVERY process the
   caller can signal (verified: `os.killpg(1, 0)` → strace shows
   `kill(-1, 0)`).

Result: the entire stack (and every other user process) receives SIGTERM;
llama-server shuts down gracefully ("exit command received" / "Received
second interrupt"), the proxy self-heals or stays down. This matches every
observed "unexplained" outage, and explains why the one-test-at-a-time run
never reproduced it (no pid=1 mock in module state).

### Not system overload
Memory/CPU/connection monitoring showed no pressure (46GB/124GB stable, no
OOM). The historical OOM kills (Jul 17/23) were a separate restart-cascade
issue. The slot scheduler also restarts the stack at 10:00/23:59 by design
(separate issue, LP-tbd).

## Fixes required

1. **Production (critical)**: `_kill_process_group` (proxy/lifecycle.py:753)
   must never call `os.killpg` with pid <= 1 (0 = own group, 1 = init, and
   via negation broadcasts to all). Validate: only killpg when `pid` is an
   int > 1. Also harden `stop_llama_server` against mock/fake processes.
2. **Test**: `test_switching_sse.py` must mock `stop_llama_server`
   (currently only `start_llama_server` is mocked) and assert it is called.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_kill_process_group` never issues `kill(-N)` with N <= 1; unit tests
      cover pid=1, pid=0, pid=None, non-int pid
- [ ] Running the full suite no longer kills the proxy stack (verified with
      a full-suite run while the proxy is up)
- [ ] test_switching_sse mocks stop_llama_server and passes
- [ ] All tests pass

## Related

- discovered-from: LP-0MS9H56R9000RIYF (test-taking-down-proxy investigation)
- related-to: LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP (GPU-wedge false positives — earlier outage cause, now fixed)
data.title: Fix _kill_process_group broadcasting SIGTERM to all processes (os.killpg(1) → kill(-1))

## Summary

Add hermetic tests in a new file `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_race.py` (following the `SimpleNamespace` fake-server pattern in `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py`) that reproduce the false-503 TOCTOU race in `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (parent LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN) and prove the lock-order fix.

## Problem context

`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py) counts `occupied_by_others` from `local_dispatch_records` under `local_dispatch_records_lock`, then nested-checks `local_active_queries >= max_local` under `local_active_queries_lock`. A concurrent `_increment_local_active_queries` (anonymous session, takes only `local_active_queries_lock`) can land between the two checks and falsely deny an explicit session that legitimately had a free slot (503 `no_slots_available`).

## Hermeticity (mandatory)

- In-process pytest only: throwaway fake server object (fresh `asyncio.Lock()`s, fresh `local_active_queries` counter, fresh `local_dispatch_records` dict), matching the pattern in `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py`.
- Must NOT send requests to a live proxy instance, must NOT depend on a live llama-server or any real backend, must not touch shared files or sockets.
- Live proxy traffic runs in a separate OS process and cannot affect the test's data.

## Approach

1. **Deterministic repro test**: force the exact interleaving (pause the explicit session between its records-count and counter-check, e.g. by holding/coordinating `local_active_queries_lock`, while an anonymous `_increment_local_active_queries` task lands). Must fail (show false 503) on the unfixed code and pass after the fix.
2. **Stress-amplification loop**: N=2 slots, 1 occupied, many concurrent `_increment_local_active_queries` tasks + repeated `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` attempts; assert zero false 503s over repeated runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A hermetic deterministic-interleaving test reproduces a false 503 (`no_slots_available`) when only 1 of N=2 slots is occupied while concurrent anonymous-session `_increment_local_active_queries` tasks run, on the current (unfixed) code.
2. A hermetic stress loop (N=2, 1 occupied, concurrent increments) produces zero false 503s after the lock-order fix, over repeated runs.
3. All tests in the new file are hermetic (in-process fake server; no live proxy, no real backend, no shared files/sockets) and pass headlessly: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_local_dispatch_race.py -q` from `proxy/`.

## Summary

Restructure `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py) to acquire `local_active_queries_lock` before `local_dispatch_records_lock` so the occupancy count and the active-counter check are atomic with respect to all counter mutators (matching the lock order already used by `_increment_local_active_queries`/`_decrement_local_active_queries`).

## Problem

`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` currently counts `occupied_by_others` from `local_dispatch_records` while holding only `local_dispatch_records_lock`, then (nested) checks `local_active_queries >= max_local` under `local_active_queries_lock`. Between those two checks a concurrent anonymous-session `_increment_local_active_queries` can increment `local_active_queries`, falsely denying an explicit session with a free slot (503 `no_slots_available`). See parent LP-0MS8ZM98R000M8AN.

## Approach

- Acquire `local_active_queries_lock` first, then `local_dispatch_records_lock` (both held for the records-count, counter-check, and increment) — consistent with the counter helpers' active-then-records order.
- Preserve all existing semantics: no-preemption policy (inactive unexpired leases reserve their slot), N-aware slot counting, expired-lease cleanup, adaptive lease timeout, legacy-mode guard (returns `(True, None, 0, 1.0)` when dispatch tracking is not initialised).
- Do NOT change the return signature: `(acquired, owner, active_count, retry_after)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` acquires `local_active_queries_lock` before `local_dispatch_records_lock`; the occupancy count and counter check are atomic with respect to all counter mutators.
2. The hermetic stress tests (child LP-0MSAO0TX0005LQNK) pass: deterministic repro no longer yields false 503; stress loop shows zero false 503s over repeated runs.
3. No-preemption policy and N-aware slot counting are preserved: existing dispatch lease tests still pass (`python3 -m pytest tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py tests/test_local_dispatch_race.py -q` from `proxy/`), including `test_n2_allows_two_concurrent_sessions`, `test_n2_blocks_third_session`, `test_n1_backward_compatible`, `test_n3_inactive_lease_reserves_slot`.
4. No deadlock introduced: lock order is consistent with `_increment_local_active_queries`/`_decrement_local_active_queries` (active -> records).

# Intake brief: Evaluate increasing local context size (ctx-size) to serve >65K-token prompts locally

## Problem statement

The local Qwen3 slot's effective context is far smaller than the routing configuration assumes. With `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144` in models.ini and 6 slots (day schedule), each slot gets ~43.7K tokens of context (262144/6); at night (8 slots) ~32.8K. The routing thresholds (cold 60K / warm 100K) are clamped to that per-slot context, so any prompt above ~43.7K tokens is forced remote. Usage data shows most sessions exceed this: median session peak context 53,984, mean 72,641, and 60.6% of sessions peak above 43.7K. The original "65K ctx" premise of this item is stale (the 65K value in a `[global]` section was never applied — see LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1). The question is whether raising the per-slot context (by cutting slots within the 262144 native ceiling, and/or other levers) yields more sessions that run fully local without remote fallback, and at what latency/memory/concurrency cost.

## Users

Primary: the operator (rgardler) who runs the local llama-proxy on the Strix Halo iGPU, plus the pi agent sessions that depend on it. Benefit: more sessions stay local (lower latency, no remote cost, privacy), fewer fallback-induced stalls and truncations.

- As an operator, I want the majority of my pi sessions to run fully local (no fallback to remote deepseek), so that local-model utilization is high and remote costs/latency drop.
- As an operator, I want a data-backed recommendation on the slot-count vs per-slot-context tradeoff (e.g. 6×43.7K, 4×65.5K, 3×87.4K, 2×131K) before changing production config, since a wrong choice would either truncate big prompts or starve concurrent sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Benchmark data**: prefill throughput (t/s), TTFT and P95 are measured for representative prompt sizes (~30K/60K/90K/120K tokens) at the baseline (6 slots × ~43.7K) and at least two candidate configs (e.g. 4×~65.5K and 3×~87.4K) using the `proxy/benchmarks` harness; results recorded as a benchmark JSON + summary in the work item.
2. **KV-cache memory**: memory per slot is measured/estimated at each candidate ctx (llama-server metrics, `/props`, rocm-smi/admin metrics) and compared against available headroom; the "~71GB available" claim from the original description is verified or corrected.
3. **Session-retention projection**: using the proxy-usage reports (379 sessions, 24h window, `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` + CSVs), the share of sessions that would stay fully local (no fallback) is computed for each candidate config vs the current baseline, and the recommendation maximizes full-local sessions (operator goal — slot reduction acceptable if it increases full-local sessions overall).
4. **Recommendation artifact**: a written go/no-go recommendation with: chosen slots×ctx, updated `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold` / `warm_cache_threshold` values, the interplay with `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` (KV persistence is currently skipped above 12,288 prompt tokens — LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO), and expected change in fallback rate. Implementation/rollout, if adopted, is tracked as a separate follow-up work item (out of scope here).
5. **Validation & docs**: benchmark runs are reproducible via `proxy/benchmarks`; the full project test suite passes; all related documentation (models.ini comments, proxy/config.yaml comments, benchmark README, docs/llama-router.md as applicable) is updated to reflect the findings and any corrected context assumptions.

> Note: CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the docs requirement — it is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Model-native context ceiling: Qwen3 `ctx-size = 262144`; per-slot = 262144 / active slots. Rope-scaling beyond native is not assumed to be in scope; if considered, quality degradation must be flagged as a risk, not silently accepted.
- Slot pool must stay aligned with llama-server `--parallel` and the `slot_schedule` (6 day / 8 night) via `session_slot_pool_size` (LP-0MSAOQTJT000S722 deliberately raised slots 4→6 for contention; the evaluation must trade this against capacity).
- Output-token headroom is reserved below the per-slot context; effective usable context is per-slot minus completion headroom (provider.py clamp, LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1).
- `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 12288` skips slot save/restore above 12.3K prompt tokens; larger contexts are never persisted, so warm-cache reuse only happens within a slot lease. This interacts directly with any ctx increase.
- Evaluation must not destabilize the live proxy: candidate configs measured via `--ctx-size` overrides / dedicated benchmark runs; production restart only if a rollout is separately approved.
- The 150K–480K prompt sub-cluster of HTTP 400 fallbacks is tracked in LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K and is out of scope (no feasible local ctx covers it).

## Existing state

- **PRODUCTION CHANGE APPLIED 2026-08-02 (operator decision, Option C — see comment LP-C0MSCA9RF1007OAQQ):** models.ini `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 131072`; config.yaml `local_model_ctx_size: 131072`, `session_slot_pool_size: 3`, schedule entries both →3 slots (uniform day/night); `start-llama.sh` router now passes `--threads 8`. Running: `--parallel 3` → per-slot ~43.7K (same day capacity as before; night improved from 32.8K). Effective routing threshold = 131072/3 − 4096 = **39594**.
- Prior state (historical): models.ini `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144`; config.yaml `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, cold threshold 60000, warm threshold 100000, `session_slot_pool_size: 6`, schedule 23:59→8 / 10:00→6, `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 12288`; router `--parallel 6` → per-slot ~43.7K day / ~32.8K night.
- **Key operational finding:** an intermediate change to ctx 65536 with 6 slots collapsed the routing threshold to 6826 (65536//6 − 4096) and forced ALL traffic remote via `warm_cache_bypass` — any future ctx/slot change must keep models.ini ctx, `local_model_ctx_size`, `session_slot_pool_size` and the schedule mutually consistent.
- Routing clamp (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`): effective thresholds = min(configured, per-slot ctx − headroom); oversized prompts fall through to remote before context exhaustion.
- 24h usage report (2026-08-01 19:52 → 08-02 19:52, 379 sessions): 76.0% of sessions fell back local→remote; fallback reasons — warm_cache_bypass 55.4%, local_concurrency_limit 18.4%, local_lease_active 12.4%, HTTP 400 9.0%, large_context_bypass 4.6%, slot_exhaustion 0.1%. Session peak-context: median 53,984 / mean 72,641 / p90 149,077 / max 480,381; 60.6% of sessions peak > 43.7K, 38.9% > 65.5K, 23.0% > 87.4K.

## Desired change

Produce the evaluation and recommendation for the FURTHER step. **Note: the operator overrode the original "no production config change" scope on 2026-08-02 and directed Option C (3×~43.7K, ctx 131072) to be implemented immediately — it is live (see comment LP-C0MSCA9RF1007OAQQ).** The remaining deliverable is benchmark data, memory accounting, and a session-retention projection for the candidate configs that raise per-slot context further (4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K), plus a written go/no-go recommendation for that further step. The original "if go" condition for C has been satisfied; F6 now recommends whether to go beyond C.

## Key Files:

- `models.ini` — `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144`; the ceiling that constrains per-slot context.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — `local_model_ctx_size`, `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`, `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, `session_slot_pool_size`, `slot_schedule`, `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — large-context routing clamp (`per_slot = ctx_size // slots`, effective threshold = min(configured, per-slot − headroom)).
- `proxy/benchmarks/run_benchmark.py`, `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` — existing benchmark harness for TTFT/throughput/memory measurement.
- `docs/llama-router.md` — router/context documentation updated by AC 5.
- `start-llama.sh` — derives `LLAMA_PARALLEL` from `session_slot_pool_size`; `--ctx-size` override point for candidate runs.
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md`, `daytime_sessions.csv`, `nighttime_sessions.csv` — the 24h usage data used for the session-retention projection.

## Related work

- LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 — models.ini `[global]` ctx-size never applied; established the per-slot clamp. The "65K" premise of this item is corrected by that finding.
- LP-0MSAOQTJT000S722 — raised cold-cache threshold 30K→60K and slot pool 4→6; the slot-count side of the tradeoff.
- LP-0MQMH0GJR001NG0B — centralized quantization/ctx-size in models.ini (plumbing for any future change).
- LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K — HTTP 400 fallback cluster; deferred the 150K–480K prompt sub-cluster to this item (related-to).
- LP-0MSAU6MKS008K0RJ — proxy usage analysis skill that produces `~/proxy-usage-reports/` (data source).
- LP-0MRGUJ3QR002K18G — slot release on remote fallback (concurrency behavior relevant to the slot-count tradeoff).
- LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO — slot persistence safeguards (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` interplay).
- LP-0MQMH11AO002IIID — GPU VRAM/ROCm metrics in Prometheus/Grafana; provides the memory-measurement tooling for AC 2.
- LP-0MRO1CM5A008R2KX — proxy progress logging only monitored slot 0; relevant if per-slot monitoring is needed during candidate benchmarks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Stale premise (known)**: the item's "currently 65000 ctx" is wrong; the real baseline is ~43.7K/slot (6 slots). ACs reference the verified baseline; a follow-up context correction is part of this intake.
- **Contention tradeoff**: cutting slots (6→4→3) may raise `local_concurrency_limit`/`local_lease_active` fallbacks (49% of session fallbacks today). Net full-local session gain must be measured, not assumed.
- **warm_cache_bypass dominance**: 55.4% of fallbacks are warm-cache bypass; because `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens=12288` prevents persistence above 12.3K, bigger ctx may not help cold sessions unless the persistence cap or lease-warmth behavior is also considered — the recommendation must address this.
- **Memory headroom**: "~71GB available" is unverified (rocm-smi reports limited VRAM on this iGPU setup); must be re-measured during the evaluation.
- **Rope-scaling**: beyond-native context extension degrades output quality and is out of scope unless explicitly requested.
- **Scope-creep guard**: implementation/rollout, HTTP 400 sub-cluster, and any persistence-cap changes are tracked as separate work items, not expanded here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should closing this item include implementing the change (models.ini/config edit, restart, monitor) once benchmarks justify it, or is the deliverable an evaluation + recommendation (benchmark data, slot/ctx tradeoff analysis, go/no-go), with implementation tracked as a separate work item?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Evaluation and recommendation." Source: interactive reply. Impact: AC 4 explicitly excludes rollout; any adoption spawns a follow-up implementation item.
- Q2: "Raising per-slot ctx >65K requires cutting slots (e.g. 4×65.5K or 3×87.4K) unless rope-scaling beyond 262144 is considered. Is reducing the day slot pool acceptable, or is rope-scaling / KV-quantization also in scope to keep 6 slots?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "The goal is maximum number of full sessions on local models (no fallback to remote) — if that means a slot reduction then so be it." Source: interactive reply. Impact: AC 3 optimizes for full-local session count; slot reduction explicitly permitted.
- Q3: "Should the target be ~65-70K/slot (covers the 69.5K median remote prompt) or ~90-100K/slot (covers the 90.7K mean)? This determines whether 4 slots suffice or 2-3 slots / rope-scaling are required." — Answer (operator, interactive): "Review the scaling reports from the usage reporting skill." Source: interactive reply + `~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md` (2026-08-02 19:52, 379 sessions). Research summary: session peak-context median 53,984 / mean 72,641 / p90 149,077; 60.6% of sessions peak > 43.7K, 38.9% > 65.5K, 23.0% > 87.4K, 13.3% > 131K. AC 3 grounds the target in these distributions rather than a fixed number; the recommendation picks the config maximizing full-local sessions.

## Summary

Tune the local LLM routing so more requests are handled by the local Qwen3 model instead of falling through to remote deepseek, with minimal latency impact.

## Context (analysis of 3h of proxy session-recordings, 2026-08-01)

Of 3,511 remote responses in the window:
- 53.5% had prompt > 65,000 tokens (cannot fit local ctx-size 65000) - tracked separately (LP ctx-size work item)
- 36.0% were 30-65K tokens: bypassed locally when the slot cache is cold due to `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold: 30000`
- 10.5% were <=30K: fell to remote due to slot/lease contention (4 slots vs 4-17 concurrent sessions in 179/180 minutes)

Local pool saturation: session_slot_pool_size 4 with the time-based schedule forcing 4 daytime slots. 65/222 local-started sessions (29%) escalated to remote; plan/code cascades escalate ~60% of the time.

## Changes

1. `local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`: 30000 -> 60000 (config.yaml, server section). One slow cold prefill per session per cache-life, amortized over force_full_prompt repeat turns; warm-cache threshold (100000) unchanged.
2. `session_slot_pool_size`: 4 -> 6 (config.yaml, server section) and matching day schedule entry (10:00 -> 6 slots; night stays 8). Requires proxy + llama-server restart (LLAMA_PARALLEL is derived from this value by lifecycle).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] config.yaml reflects threshold 60000 and pool/schedule 6 (day)
- [ ] Config parses and relevant proxy config tests pass
- [ ] After restart: llama-server runs with --parallel 6; proxy healthy
- [ ] routing_check log lines show cold_threshold=60000
- [ ] Changes committed with work item reference

data.description:
# Proxy usage analysis skill: 24h session/fallback log analysis with day-night CSVs and recommendation report

## Problem statement

Operators cannot currently tell whether the local models (llama-server via the proxy) are configured
optimally — e.g. whether slot counts (6 daytime / 8 nighttime), context limits, and routing thresholds
cause excessive fallback to remote providers, or leave local capacity idle. The data exists in the proxy
logs (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`) but there is no tool to turn the last 24 hours of session and
fallback activity into a digestible, per-session CSV record and an operator-facing recommendation report.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** (primary): wants a quick daily read on whether local models are being used well, how
  much traffic fell back to remote providers, why, and what to change.
  - *As an operator, I want a per-session breakdown of the last 24h (start/end, message count, context and
    response sizes, initial model, fallback time/reason) split into daytime (6-slot) and nighttime (8-slot)
    CSVs, so I can spot configuration problems.*
  - *As an operator, I want a single report with highlighted recommendations (e.g. raise slot pool size,
    increase ctx-size, adjust routing thresholds) backed by the captured data, so I can decide whether to
    change the local model configuration.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A skill (SKILL.md + script) exists that parses the last 24 hours of proxy logs from
   `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` including rotated files (`proxy.log.*`) that overlap the window,
   streaming large files (current `proxy.log` is >700 MB) without loading them fully into memory.
2. Running the skill produces **two CSV files** — one for daytime sessions (10:00–23:59, 6 slots) and one
   for nighttime sessions (00:00–09:59, 8 slots) — with **one row per session** covering ALL sessions in the
   window (local-only and fallback). Columns include at minimum: session id, start time, end time, duration,
   number of messages/requests, start context size, avg context size, max context size, avg response size,
   max response size, initial model assignment (provider + model), time of move to a remote model (empty if
   never fell back), and fallback reason (empty if never fell back).
3. The skill produces a **single Markdown report** that aggregates the CSVs: session/request counts, local vs
   remote split, fallback rate and reasons, per-model breakdown, daytime vs nighttime comparison, and a
   section of **highlighted recommendations** (each backed by captured data, e.g. high
   `local_concurrency_limit` fallbacks → suggest raising `session_slot_pool_size`; high
   `large_context_bypass` → suggest raising local ctx-size / `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`).
4. Log-parsing and day/night bucketing logic are covered by unit tests using fixtures derived from real log
   lines; the skill's test suite passes and the full project test suite must pass with the changes.
5. The skill is documented (SKILL.md usage instructions) and any related docs (e.g. proxy README or docs/
   usage notes) are updated to reflect the new analysis capability.

## Constraints

- Log source is read-only: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` and rotated siblings (6-hourly rotation,
  90-day retention). Must not require elevated privileges to read (currently group-readable).
- The 6/8 slot split is defined by the slot schedule in `proxy/config.yaml` (`10:00 → 6 slots`,
  `23:59 → 8 slots`) — the skill should derive day/night boundaries from that schedule, not hardcode.
- Must be safe on very large logs: streaming/line-based parsing, filter to relevant structured prefixes
  (`Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `Fallback triggered`, `routing_check`, `routing_skip_local`,
  `Session header resolved`, `lease_renewed`, `local_dispatch_denied`) rather than full-text loads.
- Log line format is text-based with `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S,%f - LEVEL - message` prefix; parsing must be
  tolerant of missing fields and truncated request payloads (payloads in log lines are cut off; token
  counts from `Stream finished ... tokens=prompt/completion/total` are authoritative for context/response
  sizes).
- No new persistent services or daemons; a single on-demand skill invocation.
- Python 3.10+, stdlib only where possible (csv, re, datetime, pathlib); no new third-party deps.

## Existing state

- Proxy logs to `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` via `TimedRotatingFileHandler` (see
  `proxy/proxy/utils.py setup_logging`), rotation every 6h, retention 90 days; the live file is currently
  >700 MB. Current process stdout also lands in `/tmp/proxy-startup.log` but the file handler is
  authoritative.
- Structured INFO lines already capture: session start/end (`Stream started/finished` with
  `provider/model/session`), per-request token counts (`tokens=prompt/completion/total`), fallback events
  (`Fallback triggered for model=..., from=..., to=..., reason=...`), routing decisions
  (`routing_check ... estimated_tokens=... messages=... cached_ratio=...`, `routing_skip_local ... reason=`),
  slot leases (`lease_renewed session=... timeout=60s`), dispatch denials (`local_dispatch_denied`).
- Full per-request payloads are also recorded under `proxy/session-recordings/<session_id>/` (request/response
  JSON with model, provider, timestamp) but the analysis can rely on log lines for the requested aggregates.
- No existing skill or tool performs this session/fallback usage analysis. `proxy/benchmarks/` covers
  performance A/B benchmarking (latency/TPS/TTFT/memory), not usage/fallback analysis.
- Slot schedule: `proxy/config.yaml` `slot_schedule` — 10:00 → 6 slots (day), 23:59 → 8 slots (night).

## Desired change

- New skill `proxy-usage-analysis` under `~/.pi/agent/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` containing:
  - `SKILL.md` — trigger description, usage instructions, output locations, interpretation guidance.
  - `scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — main entry point: discovers rotated log files overlapping the last
    24h, streams-parses the structured lines, groups by session UUID, computes per-session aggregates,
    buckets into day/night by session start time per the slot schedule, writes two CSVs and the report.
  - `scripts/...` supporting modules or inline functions for parsing, aggregation, and recommendation rules.
  - `tests/` — unit tests for parsing, session grouping, day/night bucketing, and recommendation rules,
    with fixtures copied from real log lines.
- Default output: `usage-reports/` under the project root (or configurable `--output-dir`), writing
  `daytime_sessions.csv`, `nighttime_sessions.csv`, and `report.md`; filenames may include a timestamp.
- Usage (once implemented):
  ```bash
  python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py \
      --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
      --hours 24 \
      --output-dir usage-reports
  ```
- Recommendations section generated by small rule-based heuristics backed by the captured aggregates
  (fallback-rate thresholds, dominant fallback reasons, context-size distributions vs configured
  thresholds), each recommendation citing the data that supports it.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — New skill definition with usage and interpretation guide.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` — New main analysis script (parse → group → bucket → CSV → report).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — New unit tests (parsing, bucketing, recommendations).
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` — Read-only input (no changes).
- `proxy/README.md` — Docs update target for AC 5: add a short section pointing to the new analysis skill (documented log format lives here).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — Reference only: slot schedule (10:00/23:59) and routing thresholds used by recommendations (no changes expected).
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` — Reference only: logging setup/rotation details (no changes expected).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Log format drift**: regex parsing depends on current INFO line formats (e.g. `Stream finished: reason=... tokens=a/b/c`). Mitigation: tolerant field extraction, missing-field defaults, unit tests pinned to real fixtures; if a line cannot be parsed it is counted and skipped, never fatal.
- **Very large logs**: live `proxy.log` is >700 MB and rotated siblings can exceed 1 GB. Mitigation: stream line-by-line, pre-filter by relevant prefixes, never load whole files.
- **Session boundary semantics**: a session whose start falls inside the 24h window is included even if it began before/ends after the window; day/night bucket is by session start time. Sessions spanning the 23:59 transition (drain window) may show 503s — noted in the report rather than treated as errors.
- **Authoritative token counts**: log-line request payloads are truncated; context/response sizes use `Stream finished` token counts, not payload reconstruction.
- **Scope creep**: follow-up opportunities (e.g. Grafana dashboards, alerting, per-request CSVs) are recorded as linked work items, not added to this skill's scope.

## Related work

**Summary**

Users see occasional errors: *Error: Model stopped because it reached the maximum output token limit. The response may be incomplete.* The 16K output limit (session_guardrail_max_completion_tokens: 16384) IS in effect — requests carry max_completion_tokens=16384. But real-session truncations are **not** output-limit hits; they are **context exhaustion** caused by models.ini ctx-size not being applied.

**Evidence (from /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log, 2026-08-01)**

- 23:00:34 (implement session 019fbf41, local Qwen3): prompt=43,737, completion=39, total=43,776 = **exactly the slot n_ctx** (43,776 with 6 slots). finish_reason=length.
- 22:33:16 (audit session 019fbf3a, local Qwen3): prompt=43,666, completion=110, total=43,776 = slot n_ctx. finish_reason=length.
- 23:05:40 / 23:06:34: deepseek-v4-flash @ completion_tokens=600 — these are the verify_session_caching.py test harness which explicitly sets max_tokens=600 (NOT user sessions, NOT the proxy limit).

**Root cause**

- models.ini declares `[global] ctx-size = 65000`, but llama.cpp's router preset loader only treats `[*]` sections as the global preset (common/preset.cpp:351: preset.name == "*"). `[global]` is parsed as a model named "global" with no hf-repo → ignored; its ctx-size never cascades to Qwen3.
- The `[Qwen3]` section in models.ini has no ctx-size key of its own.
- start-llama.sh router mode passes --models-preset but no --ctx-size.
- Result: Qwen3 child runs with model-native context (262,144) / slots: 6 slots → 43,776/slot; **after the 23:59 slot schedule change to 8 slots → 32,768/slot** (verified via /props on port 47779).

**Aggravating factor**

- Proxy routing thresholds assume 65K context: local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold=60000, warm=100000. Requests with estimated tokens <60K are routed to local, but the actual per-slot context is only 32,768 (now) or 43,776 (before). A 40K-token prompt passes the 60K threshold, hits local, and immediately runs out of context → llama-server returns finish_reason=length → pi UI displays the misleading "maximum output token limit" message.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Write a test that reproduces the config mismatch: parse models.ini and assert that llama.cpp router would receive ctx-size for the Qwen3 preset (e.g. via [*] section or explicit [Qwen3] ctx-size key).
2. Fix so the Qwen3 child server is launched with an explicit --ctx-size matching the intended 65000 (or whatever value fits KV memory with current slot count).
3. Align routing thresholds (cold/warm cache thresholds) with the actual per-slot context so oversized prompts fall through to remote before hitting context exhaustion.
4. Verify via /props that per-slot n_ctx matches the configured value after restart.
5. Existing tests pass (pytest in proxy/).

## Summary

The periodic dispatch cleanup loop `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py, called every ~10s from `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` in server.py) deletes expired `local_dispatch_records` entries for sessions released via `idle_timeout` and `orphan_cleanup`, but NEVER calls `_free_slot_assignment` (proxy/proxy/session.py). Only three call sites free slot registry entries:

1. router_helpers.py:780 — inline cleanup inside `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (runs only when a NEW session tries to acquire a dispatch)
2. router_helpers.py:867 — `_release_dispatch_lease` (explicit/non_explicit release path)
3. session.py:840 — `_invalidate_session_and_slot`

Sessions released through the periodic loop therefore leave permanent ghost entries in the in-memory `_slot_owners` dict. Since slots are assigned lowest-free-first, the pool eventually fills with ghosts and every new session receives `slot=none`, silently disabling proxy-level slot save/restore for the rest of the proxy's lifetime.

## Evidence (live logs 2026-08-01/02, proxy restarted 22:13:26)

- 272 periodic-loop releases since restart: 194 `reason=idle_timeout` + 78 `reason=orphan_cleanup` — none free slots.
- Session `fc29d22a` was assigned `slot=7` at 23:59:11 even though only slots 2 and 3 had ever been assigned in [local] POST logs — slots 0,1,4,5,6 were ghosted.
- Fresh verification sessions (e.g. `2d8d74b0`, `83a6f39b`, `153c604f`, `a795b28a`) consistently log `slot=none` in proxy.log despite llama-server running with `--parallel 8` and idle slots.
- Impact: session-level slot persistence (save/restore of KV snapshots) stops engaging after enough churn; the GPU-wedge fix's persistence safeguards no longer apply until proxy restart.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` frees slot registry entries for sessions it releases (idle_timeout AND orphan_cleanup branches).
- [ ] Unit test: after an idle_timeout/orphan_cleanup release, the released session's slot is available for a new session.
- [ ] Live verification: after churn, a fresh session receives `slot=N` (not `slot=none`) and `slot_save success` lines appear for it.

## Summary

The proxy's remote fallback chain (plan/author/code → deepseek/opencode) is rejected with HTTP 400 at a rate of ~1600/day (9–14% of all fallbacks). ~89% of these 400s follow assistant `tool_calls` turns with moderate token sizes, indicating the remote's strict request validation rejects the accumulated tool-call/tool-result history the proxy resends every turn (`force_full_prompt: true`). The fix: diagnose the exact rejected message shape, add observability for the 400 response body, and validate/prune the accumulated tool-call history before remote sends.

## Problem statement

Remote providers in the fallback chain return HTTP 400 for ~1600 requests/day (9–14% of all fallback events). Because the proxy silently falls back to the next provider, there is no user-visible failure — but every rejection wastes a provider call, masks a latent request-construction defect, and can degrade response quality as the chain advances. The dominant share (89.3%) follows `tool_calls` turns with moderate estimated tokens (24k–45k), pointing to remote request-validation rejections of malformed accumulated assistant-tool_calls/tool-result sequences (e.g. `content:null` + `tool_calls`, missing `tool_call_id`, truncated arguments JSON) rather than size or rate-limit causes.

## Users

- **Proxy operators** (primary) — need visibility into why the remote chain rejects requests and a durable fix so fallbacks to distant chain positions stop recurring silently.
- **End users of plan/author/code models** — benefit indirectly: fewer wasted provider hops, more consistent response quality, and lower risk of a rejection cascade when multiple chain members share the same strict validation.

### Example user stories

- As a proxy operator, I want the exact HTTP 400 response body from deepseek/opencode logged or surfaced in metrics, so I can identify the rejected field without replaying traffic by hand.
- As a proxy operator, I want the proxy to never send a message sequence with malformed tool-call artifacts (null content, dangling `tool_call_id`, truncated arguments) to a remote, so remote request validation stops rejecting valid conversation turns.
- As a proxy operator, I want a 24h usage-analysis window to show a materially lower HTTP 400 fallback share after the fix, so I can confirm the cluster is resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] RCA completed: the exact rejected message field/shape is identified by reproducing a tool-call-turn 400 against the real remote endpoint (api.deepseek.com / opencode zen), documented in the work item with the captured response body.
- [ ] Observability: the proxy logs the HTTP 400 response body snippet from remote providers (DEBUG level or a dedicated log line) and/or increments `proxy_http_errors_total{status=400, reason=...}`, so the rejection reason is discoverable without code changes.
- [ ] Fix implemented: the proxy validates/sanitizes accumulated assistant `tool_calls` + tool-result messages before sending to remote providers — malformed/empty tool-call artifacts are pruned or repaired (never sent as-is) — without altering valid tool-call semantics.
- [ ] Measurable outcome: a 24h `proxy-usage-analysis` report after deployment shows HTTP 400 fallbacks reduced by ≥50% versus the 1611/24h baseline (assumption — see Risks; target may be refined by RCA), with no increase in other fallback reasons.
- [ ] Tests: new unit tests cover the validation/pruning logic and 400-body observability; the full project test suite passes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline (`../ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js`). Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- The fallback chain must keep working: a rejected remote must still yield to the next provider; the fix must not turn silent 400s into hard request failures.
- `force_full_prompt: true` for plan/author/code models stays as configured (full history is deliberately resent every turn); the fix sanitizes the history shape rather than changing the resend policy.
- The oversized-prompt share of 400s (150k–480k prompt tokens) is **out of scope** — deferred to LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (comment LP-C0MSC1JNT8007SX00).
- Valid tool-call semantics must be preserved: avoid regressions of the class fixed by LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL and LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H (tool-call-only streams, `content` population).
- No manual CHANGELOG.md edits; no CI/CD pipeline test changes.

## Existing state

- `proxy_with_remote_fallback()` sets `fallback_reason = f"HTTP {response.status_code}"` and records attempts with a 512-char `body_snippet`, but the snippet is only included in "all providers exhausted" responses — not logged at INFO for per-fallback diagnosis (`proxy/proxy/provider.py` ~line 1606).
- `proxy_http_errors_total{endpoint,status,reason}` counter exists (`proxy/proxy/metrics.py` lines 64–65, 155–168) but is not surfaced for status=400 remote rejections.
- plan/author/code model configs all set `force_full_prompt: true` (`proxy/config.yaml` lines 129–236), so the full conversation history — including all accumulated tool-call turns — is resent every turn to opencode-go/deepseek endpoints.
- 24h evidence (1611 HTTP 400 fallbacks): 1439 (89.3%) preceded by a `Stream finished: reason=tool_calls` turn (baseline tool_calls share 60.1% → over-represented); remaining ~10% followed enormous prompts exceeding the remote context limit.

## Desired change

1. **Diagnose**: replay a failing tool-call-turn conversation to the real remote endpoint to capture the exact 400 response body and identify the rejected field (likely `content:null` + `tool_calls`, missing `tool_call_id`, or truncated arguments JSON).
2. **Observe**: add DEBUG/INFO logging of the 400 `body_snippet` and/or increment `proxy_http_errors_total{status=400}` with the fallback reason so the cluster is permanently visible in logs/metrics.
3. **Fix**: validate/sanitize the accumulated assistant `tool_calls` + tool-result message history at the point the remote request body is built (`proxy_to_remote()` / provider request path) — prune malformed tool-call artifacts, repair missing `content`/`tool_call_id`, or truncate obviously truncated arguments JSON — with unit tests.
4. **Verify**: 24h usage-analysis window shows the HTTP 400 share materially reduced; full test suite green.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — fallback loop sets `fallback_reason = f"HTTP {response.status_code}"` (~line 1606) and records `body_snippet`; add status=400 metric/DEBUG body logging; potential sanitization hook before retry.
- `proxy/proxy/proxy_remote.py` — `proxy_to_remote()` (~line 159) builds/sends remote requests; primary insertion point for request-shape validation/pruning of the message history.
- `proxy/proxy/session.py` — session message accumulation and streamed `tool_calls` collection (lines ~348–430); where malformed tool-call sequences accumulate.
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `proxy_http_errors_total` counter (lines 64–65, 155–168); surface status=400 with the fallback reason.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` / `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `force_full_prompt` decision helpers (`_should_force_full_prompt_from_config` router_helpers.py ~line 1205; `_should_force_full_prompt` lifecycle.py ~line 397) — only if the resend policy changes.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — plan/author/code `force_full_prompt: true` (lines 129–236); document or adjust if the resend policy is revisited.
- `proxy/tests/` — new unit tests for tool-call-history validation/pruning and 400-body observability.

## Related work

- **Evaluate increasing local context size (ctx-size) to serve >65K-token prompts locally (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM)** — `related-to`; owns the oversized-prompt share of 400s (150k–480k tokens); deferral comment LP-C0MSC1JNT8007SX00 added during intake.
- **Proxy usage analysis skill: 24h session/fallback log analysis (LP-0MSAU6MKS008K0RJ)** — `discovered-from`; source of the 24h evidence (~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md).
- **deepseek-v4 tool calls fail: proxy misclassifies tool-call-only streams as empty responses (LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL)** — related tool-call handling defect (completed); regression guard.
- **Fix empty content when model generates tool calls in reasoning_content (LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H)** — completed; guards against `content` population regressions.
- **RCA: occasional 'Error: Provider finish_reason: error' from remote streaming (LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C)** — related remote-chain failure RCA (open, intake_complete).
- **~/proxy-usage-reports/report.md** — 24h evidence: HTTP 400 = 957–1611 fallback events (9–14%), 89.3% tool_calls-turn preceded, 10% oversized prompts.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: HTTP 400s are caused by remote request-validation of malformed accumulated tool-call history (not auth/rate limits) — the RCA step must confirm; if another cause dominates, AC targets may need revision.
- **Risk**: pruning/sanitizing history changes what the remote model sees → behavioral drift. Mitigation: only prune malformed/empty tool-call artifacts; keep valid semantics; verify with live replays.
- **Risk**: the ≥50% reduction target is an estimate, not derived from a controlled experiment; the RCA may show a different mix. Mitigation: re-baseline against the 24h report after the fix and record actual numbers.
- **Risk**: remote free/zen tiers may have less stable validation behavior, producing 400s outside the tool-call path; the observability AC ensures these remain visible rather than silent.
- **Scope-creep risk**: observability dashboards, model-config tuning, and the ctx-size work belong to separate work items (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM) — record as linked items rather than expanding scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope of this item: should the deliverable be (a) RCA report + recommendations only, (b) RCA + observability improvement, or (c) full fix including request-shape validation/pruning of accumulated tool-call history for remote sends?" — Answer (operator): "(c) full fix including request-shape validation/pruning of accumulated tool-call history for remote sends." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "The ~10% of 400s caused by enormous prompts exceeding the remote context limit — should that be handled here, or deferred to LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM?" — Answer (operator): "defer (explicit comment in that work item)". Source: interactive reply; deferral recorded as comment LP-C0MSC1JNT8007SX00 on LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (`related-to:LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K`).

## Summary

RCA spike: reproduce the HTTP 400 fallback cluster against the real remote endpoints (opencode zen, opencode zen/go, api.deepseek.com) using minimal synthetic chat-completions payloads that mirror the tool-call-turn message shapes observed in recorded traffic (`content: null` + `tool_calls`, non-standard `reasoning_content`, missing `tool_call_id`, truncated arguments JSON). Capture the exact 400 response bodies and identify the rejected field/shape.

## Context

- Recorded traffic in `proxy/session-recordings/` shows assistant messages of the shape `{"role": "assistant", "content": null, "reasoning_content": "...", "tool_calls": [...]}` — prime reproduction templates (strip to minimal payloads first).
- Remote chain members (see `proxy/config.yaml` plan/author/code blocks): opencode-deepseek-free (opencode.ai/zen), opencode-go-2-deepseek and opencode-go-deepseek (opencode.ai/zen/go), deepseek-v4-flash (api.deepseek.com). API keys via env vars or pi auth.json.
- Operator decision (planning interview Q1): real-endpoint replay with synthetic minimal payloads only — no replay of live recorded traffic.

## User story

As a proxy operator, I want to know exactly which message field/shape causes remote HTTP 400 rejections, so the sanitizer fix can be targeted and the cluster resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] At least one synthetic tool-call-turn payload reproduces HTTP 400 on at least one real remote endpoint.
- [ ] The exact 400 response body is captured and recorded (work-item comment or notes file).
- [ ] The rejected field/shape is identified and documented for each affected provider.
- [ ] Probe count is bounded (no more than ~20 requests total, respecting provider rate limits).
- [ ] Findings are propagated to the sanitizer test and implementation feature descriptions before those are implemented.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Extract the tool-call-turn message shapes from recorded traffic as templates.
2. Reduce each to the smallest payload that still triggers validation (add/remove candidate fields one at a time).
3. POST each payload to the four remote endpoints using configured API keys.
4. Record status code and response body per shape per endpoint.
5. Summarise the rejected-field matrix in a comment on the parent work item; link from this description.

## Dependencies

- Parent: LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K
- Blocks: sanitizer tests (F4) and sanitizer implementation (F5) — via dependency edges.

## Deliverables

- Reproduction notes/script, captured 400 response bodies, rejected-shape matrix, findings comment on the parent work item.
