data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
Implemented and pushed to dev, commit `14cf1e4`.

## Changes
- **Disabled GPU-wedge detection by default**: `llama_gpu_wedge_detection_enabled` now defaults to `false` (code + `proxy/config.yaml`). On this Strix Halo APU the busy counter is pinned at 100% regardless of GPU state, so the busy+idle signature false-positives on every idle period; a wedged engine (~53W) is indistinguishable from idle (~54W) from GPU sensors on this hardware class. Documented decision recorded in config.yaml and module docstring.
- **Power-draw discrimination** (new): reads GPU power from sysfs `power1_average` (µW, amdgpu hwmon) with `rocm-smi --showpower` fallback. `_gpu_wedge_discriminate()` classifies: busy≥90 + idle slots + compute-level power → `wedge` (recover, legacy behavior preserved when power unavailable); busy + idle + low power → `pinned` (counter unreliable or stalled engine — never unloads).
- **Pinned-counter auto-disable**: N consecutive `pinned` observations (default 4, ~40s) disable busy-based detection for the process lifetime with an ERROR log; exposed as `/health` `gpu_wedge_detection_disabled`.
- **New config**: `llama_gpu_wedge_power_low_threshold_watts` (90), `llama_gpu_wedge_pinned_checks_required` (4).
- **Tests**: added `_gpu_power_draw_sysfs/_rocm_smi`, `_read_gpu_power_draw`, `_gpu_wedge_discriminate` (incl. pinned-at-100% busy + low power input), updated `_probe_gpu_wedge` (3-tuple) and /health reporting tests. 42 tests pass (`test_gpu_wedge_detection.py` + `test_tts_health_endpoint.py`).

## Acceptance criteria status
- No unload/reload during sustained idle: satisfied (detection disabled by default; pinned path never unloads).
- Genuine wedge recovery OR documented disable decision: both — decision documented; detector retained (opt-in) with power discrimination.
- In-flight requests not killed: satisfied (no spurious unloads).
- Unit tests with pinned-at-100% busy counter input: satisfied.
- 24h unload/reload count → ~0: expected once this lands on the running proxy.

data.comment:
## Diagnostic complete — NO test kills the proxy

Ran all 1528 tests one at a time (`pytest <nodeid>` per invocation), logging START/END of each and checking `GET /health` after every test. Log: `/tmp/proxy-test-diagnostic.log`.

### Results
- **1528/1528 tests ran, 0 test failures** (all rc=0), proxy process never died (0 curl failures).
- 854 health checks OK, 674 degraded — all degraded blocks caused by the GPU-wedge false-positive loop, NOT by any test.

### Root cause of the "proxy down" symptom
The running proxy (started 22:42:14) was still on **pre-fix code** (LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP fix `14cf1e4` landed at 22:43:54). With the old code, `llama_gpu_wedge_detection_enabled` was `true`, and on this APU `gpu_busy_percent` is pinned at 100% — so the wedge detector fires **whenever Qwen3 slots are idle for 2 consecutive health checks (~20s)**, which is exactly what happens during a test run (no local requests). Log evidence: `GPU wedge detected for model Qwen3 ... gpu_busy=100% with all slots idle` every ~40s (23:01:50 → 23:12:31), each cycle unloading/reloading the 23GB model and marking `/health` degraded (`gpu_wedge_detected: true`, `ready: false`). In-flight local requests get killed by the unloads — the operator-visible "proxy down".

### Remediation
- Restarted the proxy at 23:12:36 from the fixed main checkout (`14cf1e4`, `llama_gpu_wedge_detection_enabled: false`).
- Post-restart: `/health` healthy, `gpu_wedge_signal_count: 0`, **0 wedge events in 3+ min of idle** (previously 1 per ~40s).

### Conclusions
1. No test file/function takes the proxy down; the full suite is safe to run against a running proxy.
2. The earlier "proxy killed by test run" incidents were the wedge churn on pre-fix code.
3. The fix for LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP is confirmed effective on this hardware.

data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
## Refined investigation (multi-incident analysis, 23:50–23:59)

Follow-up to the one-at-a-time diagnostic. Monitored a full-suite run live
(memory/process sampling every 2s) and forensically reconstructed every
llama-server/TTS death from proxy.log + rotated llama-server logs.

### NOT memory/CPU overload
Full-suite run monitored live: memory rock-stable at 45–46GB of 124GB, no
swap pressure, no systemd-oomd kills, no kernel OOM. All deaths were
SIGTERM/exit-command shutdowns, not OOM kills (-9). Historical OOM kills
(Jul 17, Jul 23 — pre-wedge-code) killed llama-server only when 17+
llama-server instances had accumulated (restart cascade), a separate
failure mode.

### Confirmed cause 1: slot scheduler kills the stack daily
`slot_scheduler.py` calls `restart_services()` at scheduled transitions
(10:00→4 slots, 23:59→8 slots, drain=3 min). `restart_services()` stops TTS
+ llama-server (SIGTERM) and restarts. Confirmed at 23:59:00:
`restart_services: restarting llama-server with 8 slots
(reason=scheduled_slot_change)` → `Killing process group` for both TTS and
llama. This kills in-flight requests and takes the proxy down ~10s
regardless of tests; the drain window (opens 23:56) also refuses new
requests (`drain_active: refusing new request, retry_after=180s`). A test
run or agent traffic at 23:56–23:59 will observe "proxy down".

### Confirmed cause 2: restart cascades
Multiple `start-proxy.sh --restart` runs occurred around the outages:
23:51:32 (operator manual) and 23:57:17 (spawned the current stack; parent
orphaned — likely an agent session; pi agent sessions appeared 23:56:24).
Each run pkills llama-server + tts-server + uvicorn. With many agents
active, an agent (start-proxy skill) or the operator reacting to an outage
triggers a fresh kill/restart cycle.

### The two "unexplained" deaths (23:50:02, 23:56:18)
Rotated llama-server logs show GRACEFUL external shutdowns, not crashes:
- 23:50:02: `exit command received, exiting...` → models unloaded cleanly →
  `exited with status 0` (router-mode llama-server told to stop; proxy
  watchdog then saw -15).
- 23:56:18: `cleaning up before exit...` → `Received second interrupt,
  terminating immediately` (SIGINT/SIGTERM x2, mid-request).
Neither had ANY logged proxy-internal trigger (no restart_services, no
model_health recovery, no watchdog unhealthy-worker, no stop_llama_server
log). Both were external stop signals to the llama-server process.

### Tests are not the cause
- 1528 tests run one-at-a-time: zero incidents.
- Connection-pool tests (test_stale_connection_pool, test_httpx_pooling)
  use ephemeral in-process servers, NOT the live proxy.
- No test spawns/kills real processes (all lifecycle/tts tests mocked).

### Conclusions
1. No memory/CPU/connection-count overload from running tests was
   observed; the deaths are deliberate SIGTERM/exit-command shutdowns.
2. The slot scheduler is a CONFIRMED culprit for scheduled outages and
   mid-run proxy deaths around 23:56–23:59 / 10:00.
3. Restart cascades (agents/operator reacting to outages) amplify the
   downtime.
4. The exact sender of the external stop signals at 23:50:02/23:56:18 is
   not identifiable from logs — next step is live instrumentation (strace
   on the router llama-server for signal delivery + correlating agent
   session logs at the death instant).

data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
## Final RCA — resolved

Root cause of "test suite kills the proxy": TWO bugs in the suite, both
strace-confirmed and both fixed (commit `65e4646`, see LP-0MS9LJIAE008Q3AK):

1. **`os.killpg(1, SIGTERM)` → `kill(-1, SIGTERM)` system-wide broadcast**
   (test_switching_sse → unmocked `stop_llama_server()` → `_kill_process_group`
   with a pid=1 fake llama_process left in module state). Fixed with a pid
   guard in `_kill_process_group` + mocking `stop_llama_server` in the test.
2. **Leaked real watchdog loops** (test_tts_watchdog started
   `_startup_launch_watchdog_tasks()` and never cancelled `model_health_task`;
   the loop later ran port-based zombie cleanup / recovery against the live
   stack). Fixed with inert loops + cancelling all three tasks.

Not the cause: memory/CPU/connection overload (live-monitored: 46GB/124GB
stable, no OOM; deaths were deliberate signals, not overload). The
slot scheduler's daily scheduled restarts (10:00/23:59) are a separate
by-design behavior.

Verification: post-fix full-suite run under strace showed **zero** kill
syscalls from pytest; the suite completed (1531 passed, 4 flaky) with the
proxy healthy throughout.

Implemented and pushed to dev, commit `65e4646`.

## Fixes
1. **Production (critical)**: `_kill_process_group` (proxy/lifecycle.py) now
   refuses `pid <= 1` / non-int / bool pids before `os.killpg`. Python's
   `os.killpg(1, SIGTERM)` negates the pgid and issues `kill(-1, SIGTERM)` —
   a system-wide broadcast. Verified under strace: run4 showed the pytest
   process issuing `kill(-1, SIGTERM)`; a pid=1 fake llama_process (left in
   module state by test fixtures) triggered it via the unmocked
   `stop_llama_server()` path in test_switching_sse.
2. **Test**: test_switching_sse now mocks `stop_llama_server` (was only
   mocking `start_llama_server`) and asserts it is called.
3. **Test**: test_tts_watchdog::test_watchdog_task_launched_on_startup was
   starting the REAL watchdog loops (`_startup_launch_watchdog_tasks`) and
   never cancelling `model_health_task`; the leaked loop ran port-based
   zombie cleanup / unload-reload recovery against the live stack ~10s
   later. Now uses inert loop stand-ins and cancels ALL three tasks.
4. **New tests**: tests/test_kill_process_group.py covers pid 1/0/None/
   bool/non-int.

## Verification
- run4 (pre-fix, pytest under strace): `kill(-1, SIGTERM)` from pytest.
- run7 (post-fix, pytest under strace): **zero** kill syscalls from pytest.
- run8 (final): full suite completed — 1531 passed, 4 failed (all flaky,
  pass on re-run: max_tokens_truncation_warning x2, version_footer x2),
  3 skipped — and the proxy stayed healthy throughout.

data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
## Final verification (run9, fully instrumented)

Ran the full suite again with BOTH the stack and pytest under strace:
- Suite COMPLETED: 1531 passed, 3 skipped, 4 failed (same flaky tests —
  test_max_tokens_truncation_warning x2, test_version_footer x2; all pass
  on re-run).
- **pytest made ZERO kill syscalls** (no kill(-N), no SIGTERM broadcast).
- **Zero llama-server/TTS deaths during the entire run** — proxy healthy
  throughout (the only signals captured were benign startup kills).

The residual death in run8 (~30s after suite end) did NOT recur in run9 —
run8 ran while another agent was active on the machine; the operator
stopped it before run9. Conclusion: the test suite no longer kills the
proxy (strace-verified); residual environmental kills correlate with other
agent activity, not the suite.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
# Findings: operational ctx-size change 2026-08-02 (operator-directed)

## What happened (chronology)

1. **Performance investigation** — observed Qwen3 llama-server pegged at ~200% CPU, GPU 100% busy on the Strix Halo iGPU (shared LPDDR5X memory bus with the CPU). Root cause: memory-bandwidth contention, not CPU compute. Config change to reduce bandwidth pressure was requested by the operator.
2. **First change (reverted by evidence): ctx 262144→65536, threads 16→8** — this BROKE local routing entirely. Every request started falling through to remote (`opencode-go-2-deepseek`) with `reason=warm_cache_bypass`. All 6 slots sat idle; local Qwen3 utilization dropped to ~0%.
3. **Root cause of the breakage (the key finding):** the routing clamp in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_effective_large_context_thresholds`) computes:

   ```
   per_slot = local_model_ctx_size // active_slots
   cap      = per_slot - _LOCAL_ROUTING_OUTPUT_HEADROOM (4096)
   effective_threshold = min(configured_cold/warm, cap)
   ```

   With `local_model_ctx_size: 65536` and 6 active slots → per_slot 10922, cap **6826**. Configured cold=60000/warm=100000 were clamped down to 6826. Agent sessions carry 17K–62K estimated tokens, so every request exceeded the clamp and was deliberately bypassed to remote (the bypass is intentional — it prevents KV-slot truncation, LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1).
4. **Fix chosen by operator (Option C): ctx 131072 + 3 slots.** Per-slot context = 131072/3 = 43690; effective routing threshold = **39594** (restores the original day-baseline per-slot capacity, ~43.7K, with half the total KV footprint and less bus contention).

## Changes applied (all live, proxy restarted 21:57 UTC)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `models.ini` | `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 65536` → `131072` |
| `proxy/config.yaml` | `local_model_ctx_size: 65536` → `131072` |
| `proxy/config.yaml` | `session_slot_pool_size: 6` → `3` |
| `proxy/config.yaml` | `slot_schedule` entries: `23:59→8`, `10:00→6` → both `→3` (schedule must match `--parallel`; the live clamp reads the scheduler, not the static value) |
| `start-llama.sh` | added `--threads "${LLAMA_THREADS:-8}"` to the router cmd (propagates to all child workers via preset merge) |

Verified live: router `--parallel 3`, Qwen3 worker `--ctx-size 131072 --threads 8`, threshold = 39594 in routing logs. 20K–31K-token prompts route local again (prefill 350–425 tok/s); 95K-token prompts correctly bypass to remote.

## Resource effect

- Recurrent-state KV memory halved vs the 6-slot baseline (3 cells vs 6 cells; 188 MiB vs 377 MiB recurrent buffers for the 40-layer recurrent model).
- Concurrent local slots: 6 → 3 (day and night). Beyond 3 concurrent local sessions, traffic falls through to remote (existing `local_concurrency_limit` fallback) — acceptable per operator (max full-local sessions, slot reduction explicitly permitted, Q2 in intake appendix).
- Night capacity IMPROVED vs the old 8-slot schedule: per-slot context at night was 262144/8 ≈ 32.8K (threshold ~28.7K); now 3×43.7K (threshold ~39.6K) at all times.

## Impact on this evaluation plan (children F1–F7)

- **This item's scope said "no production config change"** — the operator explicitly overrode that by directing Option C to be implemented now. The evaluation's remaining open questions (does raising per-slot context further to 65.5K/87.4K/131K buy more fully-local sessions) are unchanged and still worth benchmarking.
- **F2 (baseline benchmarks)**: live day baseline is no longer 6×43.7K — it is now **3×43.7K** (day AND night, uniform schedule). Old 6×43.7K / 8×32.8K baselines are historical; F2 should re-baseline against the live 3×43.7K config.
- **F3 (candidate benchmarks)**: Option C (3×43.7K, ctx 131072) is NOT in the planned candidate set (4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K at ctx 262144). The candidates still measure the "more per-slot context" tradeoff and remain open. C is the restored-capacity control point; candidates are the capacity-increase experiments.
- **F6 (go/no-go recommendation)**: the go decision for C has been made by the operator and implemented. F6 should now produce the recommendation for the FURTHER step (whether 4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K is worth the additional slot reduction), grounded in the F2/F3/F4/F5 data.
- **F4 (memory accounting)**: measured numbers above (188 MiB recurrent, 3 slots) provide the C data point.
- **F5 (session-retention projection)**: retention for C equals the historical day baseline (~39.4% of sessions ≤43.7K peak stay fully local, per the 24h usage report) with night improved. Re-run projection against the new baseline before deciding on further candidates.
- **Not changed** (out of scope): `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens: 12288` persistence cap (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO interplay still applies), rope-scaling, HTTP 400 sub-cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).

## Prevention note

Any future change to `ctx-size` or slot count MUST keep `models.ini` ctx, `config.yaml local_model_ctx_size`, `session_slot_pool_size`, and `slot_schedule` entries mutually consistent — a mismatch collapses the routing threshold and silently moves ALL traffic to remote (exactly what happened here). Consider a config-validation test (or startup assertion) that checks `local_model_ctx_size // scheduler_slots - 4096 >= some_minimum` (e.g. 10K) as a follow-up improvement.

data.comment:
# Option 1 (ctx 262144 / 4 slots) — live performance findings (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM)

## Config verified live
- `[Qwen3] ctx-size = 262144`, `local_model_ctx_size: 262144`, `session_slot_pool_size: 4`, schedule 4/4, `--threads 8`
- llama-server: `n_ctx=262144`, `n_ctx_seq=65536` (4 slots), KV 5120 MiB (65536 cells, 10 layers, 4/4 seqs)
- Routing clamp live: cold 60000 / warm 61440 (262144//4 − 4096) — 627 checks at 61440 confirmed

## Impact vs Option C (3×43.7K) — 23:02–23:31 IST, same live workload (~40 unique sessions)

| Metric | Option C (47 min) | Option 1 (29 min) |
|---|---|---|
| Local stream completions | 99 | **6** |
| Local POSTs submitted | 146 | 223 |
| Remote (opencode) completions | 46 | 50 |
| local_concurrency_limit fallbacks | 434 | 427 |
| warm_cache_bypass | 0 | 401 (legit >61K prompts) |
| Generation speed (typical) | 12–17 tok/s | **0.16–0.19 tok/s** |
| Prefill (20–31K prompt) | 350–425 tok/s | 169–199 tok/s |
| Median prompt size routed local | 31.9K | 58.8K |

## Root cause
1. **Bigger per-slot ctx admits heavy prompts**: threshold rose 39594 → 61440, so 30–60K-token prompts now route local. Median local prompt size nearly doubled (31.9K → 58.8K).
2. **Generation over large contexts is pathologically slow on the iGPU**: hybrid/recurrent attention over 40–60K context at ~0.2 tok/s; llama-server log shows "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent)" on every slot handoff.
3. **Slot churn under load**: ~40 unique sessions competing for 4 slots with 3s idle timeout → constant slot release/re-acquire → full re-prefill each time (163s for a 27K prompt). GPU at 100% mostly doing re-prefills, starving generation.
4. Concurrency fallbacks unchanged (427 vs 434) — 4 slots didn't relieve the pool exhaustion because each slot now spends 10+ min per large generation instead of ~30s.

## Verdict
Option 1 is a **regression** for the current workload. Local throughput collapsed 16× (6 vs 99 completions), generation speed dropped ~100× (0.16 vs 12–17 tok/s), and concurrency fallbacks stayed flat. The routing clamp works as designed (no all-remote bug), but the larger context is a net negative on this hardware.

## Recommendation
- Revert to Option C (131072/3, threshold 39594) which had usable generation (12–17 tok/s) and 99 local completions, OR
- Investigate `session_slot_timeout_seconds` (3.0s): with ~40 churning sessions, the timeout forces constant slot release → re-prefill storms. Raising it (e.g. 60–300s) may pin sessions to slots and cut re-prefill cost. This is a separate lever from ctx/slots (track as new child if pursued).
- F2/F3 benchmark candidates 4×65.5K now has live data: it does NOT help; 3×87.4K and 2×131K would admit even bigger contexts and likely be worse. F6 recommendation should reflect this.

## Correction (2026-08-02) — cold-cache confound in the Option-1 live test

Comment LP-C0MSCDW1E5005GVFM reported Option 1 (262144/4) as a regression vs Option C based on live data 23:02–23:31. **That verdict is provisional and likely confounded by cold caches.** Both restarts (21:57 Option C, 23:02 Option 1) started with empty slot caches; llama-server logs "forcing full prompt re-processing due to lack of cache data (likely due to SWA or hybrid/recurrent)" during the transient. Option C was measured 18–65 min after its restart (warm); Option 1 was measured 0–29 min after (cold). The observed 0.16–0.19 tok/s generation and 6 local completions fall inside the cold-cache re-prefill storm and cannot be attributed to the config.

**Action taken:** F1 (LP-0MSC95VTC008GVR7), F2 (LP-0MSC95VX1009RBDS), and F3 (LP-0MSC95W0H0003JOL) now mandate a two-phase benchmark protocol — cold-start transient AND warm steady-state (≥30 min live traffic or ≥20 completed local turns) — with `--clean-cache` default off and restart timestamps recorded. F3 explicitly requires 4×65.5K to be judged on steady-state data, not cold-start.

data.comment:
## Option 1 (262144/4) settled-period evaluation (2026-08-03 00:45 IST)

Window: 23:30–00:45 (75 min), ~1h after restart, past cold-cache transient. Restart at 23:02:39; config verified live: n_ctx=262144, n_ctx_seq=65536 (4 slots), threshold cold 60000/warm 61440 (98 routing checks confirmed).

### What works
- Routing clamp correct and stable: only 66 warm_cache_bypass in settled period (legit >61.4K prompts) vs 401 in cold transient. No all-remote bug.

### What limits performance
1. **Concurrency is the binding constraint**: 921 local_concurrency_limit fallbacks in settled period (dominant remote driver). 9 active pi sessions vs 4 slots. Option 1 did not relieve pool exhaustion — each occupant holds a slot longer.
2. **Large prefills serialize the GPU**: 8 prefills ≥11.7K tokens, 6 ≥26K: 46.7K→444s, 47.2K→329s, 34K→207s, 28K→197s. Total 26.4 min pure prefill in ~105 min wall. During each, other slots drop to 0.16–2.8 tok/s.
3. **Generation bimodal**: 25–35 tok/s (small ctx, uncontended) vs 0.16–2.8 tok/s (during prefill storms). Config-intrinsic — raising threshold admits 40–60K prompts whose prefills dominate the iGPU.
4. **User-visible latency (local streams, n=15)**: median 76s, p90 23 min, max 30 min. 33% of completions >5 min.
5. **Local utilization**: 16 local vs 104 remote completions (13% local share) in settled window.

### Interpretation
Both limiters push traffic remote: slot scarcity (4 vs 9 sessions → 921 concurrency fallbacks) and slow big-context service (p90 23 min). The larger per-slot context did not deliver more local sessions in practice because (a) concurrency fell 6→4 and (b) 40–60K prefills monopolize the GPU. Data feeds F6 recommendation; candidate 3×87.4K / 2×131K would admit even bigger contexts and likely worse. Compare vs Option C warm data (median prompt 31.9K, prefills 350–425 tok/s, 12–17 tok/s generation) — those numbers were also partially cold-confounded, so the F2/F3 two-phase sweeps remain the authoritative comparison.

data.comment:
**F6 recommendation (LP-0MSC95WB5009U9S0) — NO-GO on further capacity increase; stay on live 3×43.7K (Option C).**

## Decision
Do NOT advance to 4×65.5K / 3×87.4K / 2×131K. The live 3×43.7K (131072/3, Option C, already operator-approved & implemented per LP-C0MSCA9RF1007OAQQ) remains the recommended config. Evidence from F2-F5:

## Evidence

| Criterion | 3x43.7K (live) | 4x65.5K | 3x87.4K | 2x131K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60K local prefill | N/A (bypass) | 400→remote (77K>65536 slot) | local 616s cold / TIMEOUT warm | local ~598s cold+warm |
| context-only full-local (F5) | 21.5% | 29.0% | 31.7% | 33.3% |
| concurrency-aware expected (F5) | 3.1% | **5.5%** | 4.5% | 3.2% |
| raised-cap full-local (F5) | 51.6% | 74.2% | 82.3% | 88.7% |
| KV memory (F4) | 1362 MiB | 2720 MiB | 2725 MiB | 2720 MiB |

## Rationale

1. **Concurrency is the binding constraint** (F5, confirms LP-C0MSCGC2W0001FNJE): peak 21 concurrent sessions vs 2-4 slots → expected full-local retention 3-5.5% for ALL configs. The best candidate (4x65.5K, 5.5%) is still ~95% remote. Slot count drives retention more than context size; 2x131K's bigger context is cancelled by 2 slots (worst 3.2%).
2. **Large local prefill is operationally impractical** (F3): a 60K prompt takes ~10 min to prefill locally (599-616s) in cold AND warm — prefill-bound, not cache-bound. 3x87.4K warm even TIMED OUT (1200s) due to dispatch-lease orphan_cleanup restarting the prefill. Any config admitting >40K prompts exposes this.
3. **Memory is a non-issue** (F4): all candidates fit with ~60 GiB headroom; KV delta is only +1.36 GiB vs baseline. Memory does not justify any candidate.
4. **Routing-estimate tokenizer mismatch** (F2/F3): tiktoken undercounts Qwen3 tokens 1.69× — 4x65.5K admits the 60K fixture (est 45357 < clamp 61440) but actual 77K > 65536 slot → 400→remote. Effective local capacity is ~39K tokens of dense prose regardless of slot size until the estimator is fixed.

## Threshold recommendations
- Keep cold 60000 / warm 61440 for the live config (or clamp-derived per-slot−4096).
- **Raise session_slot_max_prompt_tokens (12288 → per-slot clamp) as the higher-leverage change**: raises context-only full-local from 51.6% to 88.7% (2x131K) — but concurrency still caps realized retention.

## Expected delta in fallback rate
- Staying on 3x43.7K: no change (baseline).
- Advancing to 4x65.5K: +2.4pp concurrency-aware retention (3.1%→5.5%) — marginal, not worth the 60K-400 behavior.
- Follow-up recommendation: fix the routing estimator (native tokenizer or multiplier) + raise persistence cap; re-evaluate candidates only after.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
**Follow-up on F3 lease hazard (operator question: 'should we increase the lease time?').**

**Answer: No — raising the base lease timeout is the wrong fix.** The F3 60K timeout (3x87.4K warm) was caused by an **anonymous-session gap**, not an insufficient timeout value:

1. The benchmark request has no session header -> `session_explicit=False`.
2. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (router.py:717), which applies the **adaptive lease** (base 60 + est_tokens x 0.015, cap 1500 = ~740s for the 60K fixture), is gated by `if session_id and session_explicit` — anonymous requests get the default 60s.
3. The 600s prefill produced no stream chunks to refresh the lease -> 10s cleanup loop orphan-cleaned it at 62s -> prefill restarted -> timeout.

Raising the base 60s lease would reintroduce the cross-session blocking that LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P deliberately removed (180s->60s). **The surgical fix is to apply the existing adaptive lease to anonymous mid-prefill requests** (or refresh by KV progress). Tracked in **LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI**.

Real production impact is lower than the benchmark suggests: pi/agent sessions send explicit headers and already get the adaptive lease; the gap hits anonymous one-shot requests (curl/integrations).

data.comment: Discovered during log investigation (user-reported 'Model stopped because it reached the maximum output token limit'). The 16K max_completion_tokens IS in effect (requests carry max_completion_tokens=16384), but real-session truncations on local Qwen3 are **context exhaustion**, not output-limit hits: e.g. 23:00:34 prompt=43,737 + completion=39 = 43,776 = exactly slot n_ctx (6 slots); 22:33:16 prompt=43,666 + 110 = 43,776. llama.cpp router ignores [global] sections (only [*] is the global preset), so models.ini ctx-size=65000 never reaches the Qwen3 child — it runs with native 262144/slots = 43,776 (6 slots) or 32,768 (8 slots after 23:59 schedule change). Routing thresholds (cold=60000/warm=100000) assume 65K ctx, so oversized prompts are still routed local and immediately truncate. Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (evaluate raising ctx). See log lines 7197010-7197012, 6820477-6820478, 7320966, 7335564 in /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.

Routing site now clamps cold/warm thresholds to actual per-slot context (ctx_size / active_slots, schedule-aware, minus 4096 output headroom) so prompts that cannot fit the KV slot fall through to remote BEFORE context exhaustion.

## Implementation complete — pushed to dev

All 6 children implemented, tested, and pushed to `dev` (branch wl-LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K-http400-fallback). Full proxy test suite: **1580 passed, 4 skipped (env-gated live E2E), 0 failures**.

### Commits (29462fb..02350a4 on dev)

| Commit | Child | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| c104e53 | F1 (RCA) | Probe script + report: real-endpoint replay confirms 400 shapes |
| 6c18e43 | F2 (tests) | Red tests: 400-body observability (log snippet + metric) |

| f62ca31 | F4 (tests) | Red tests: tool-call history sanitizer |
| 02350a4 | F5 (sanitizer) | `_sanitize_remote_messages` in proxy_remote.py: always-on, hybrid repair/prune |

### RCA conclusion (F1)

HTTP 400 rejections are strict request-validation failures of malformed tool-call/tool-result sequences — **not** content:null, reasoning_content, or truncated arguments (those are accepted by the real endpoints). Rejected shapes (confirmed 400 on both opencode zen/go and api.deepseek.com):

- tool message missing `tool_call_id`
- dangling/mismatched `tool_call_id`
- assistant tool_calls entry missing `id`
- empty `tool_calls` array

### Fix

`_sanitize_remote_messages` (always-on, no config flag, called from `proxy_to_remote`): repairs content:null→'', missing type→'function', missing arguments→''; prunes missing/dangling tool_call_id, missing id, empty tool_calls; strips reasoning_content; preserves truncated arguments and valid sequences (regression-guarded against LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL / LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H). Mutations logged at DEBUG.

### Verification status

- In-session: suite green, docs updated (README observability + sanitizer sections).
- 24h post-deployment measurement pending (F6): baseline HTTP 400 = 938/24h (9.0% of fallbacks); procedure documented on F6; expect ≥50% reduction (target ≤~469).

## RCA Findings (F1 complete)

Probed 3 real endpoints with 24 synthetic minimal payloads (20 + 4 follow-up, bounded per AC). Full report: `proxy/scripts/rca_http400_probe_report.json` (committed with F1).

### Rejected-shape matrix (400 responses)

| Shape | opencode.ai/zen (free) | opencode.ai/zen/go | api.deepseek.com |
|---|---|---|---|
| control (valid) | 429 rate-limit | 200 OK | 200 OK |
| content:null + tool_calls | 429 | 200 OK | 200 OK |
| content:null + reasoning_content + tool_calls | 429 | 200 OK | 200 OK |
| **missing tool_call_id** | 429 | **400** | **400** |
| **mismatched/dangling tool_call_id** | 429 | **400** | **400** |
| **missing id/type on tool_calls entry** | 429 | **400** | **400** |
| truncated arguments JSON | 429 | 200 OK | 200 OK |
| **empty tool_calls array** | 429 | **400** | **400** |

### Key conclusions

1. **Root cause confirmed**: HTTP 400 rejections are strict request-validation rejections of malformed tool-call/tool-result sequences — NOT content:null, NOT truncated arguments, NOT size (at these sizes). The recorded shape `{"role":"assistant","content":null,"reasoning_content":"...","tool_calls":[...]}` is ACCEPTED by both zen/go and deepseek — content:null + reasoning_content are not the trigger.
2. **Rejected fields** (exact error bodies captured):
   - `messages[i]: missing field 'tool_call_id'` on tool messages (both zen/go and deepseek) — deserialize failure
   - `An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'` (both) — dangling references
   - `messages[i]: missing field 'id'` on tool_calls entries (both)
   - `Invalid 'messages[i].tool_calls': empty array. Expected minimum length 1` (both)
3. **opencode.ai/zen free tier** returned 429 FreeUsageLimitError for ALL shapes during the probe window — that endpoint is rate-limited (matches the existing free_usage_limit path), so 400s there were not reproducible today; the opencode-go + deepseek results are the actionable ones. The 400 cluster (~1600/day) is dominated by tool_calls-turn follows on the non-free chain members.
4. **Sanitizer target set**: prune/repair messages with missing tool_call_id, dangling tool_call_id, missing id/type, empty tool_calls — always-on, hybrid policy (repair where unambiguous, prune where not).

Findings propagated to F4 (sanitizer tests) and F5 (sanitizer impl) descriptions.

**F3 progress — 3×87.4K warm phase done (1 timeout).** JSON: `candidate_3x87.4K_q8_warm.json` (3/4 completed).

| Size | Routing | Warm result |
|---|---|---|
| 30k (38529) | local | 14.1s, 9.05 tps |
| 60k (~77K actual) | **local** | **TIMEOUT 1200s** — prefill only reached ~80% (65536/77060) when client gave up |
| 90k | large_context_bypass (cold thr) → remote | 4.8s |
| 120k | warm_cache_bypass → remote | 8.3s |

**Critical findings (3×87.4K):**
1. **Large local prefill is impractical even warm**: 60K local prefill took >20 min (1200s timeout) and never completed. Cold it took 616s; warm it was WORSE because the proxy's orphan_cleanup released the dispatch lease mid-prefill (04:08:32, ~62s after dispatch), forcing a prefill restart. The 2-min+ prefill exceeds lease cleanup expectations.
2. **Orphan_cleanup vs large-prefill interaction (new)**: dispatch_cleanup treats long-running local prefills as orphaned streams and releases their leases → prefill restart → effective 2× slowdown. This is an operational bug risk for ANY config admitting >40K local prompts.
3. 90K fixture bypasses via the COLD threshold (60000) for fresh sessions even though est 67975 < warm cap 83285 — the cold/warm split means only cached large sessions get local 90K service.

Cold phase earlier: 60K local 616s (0.21 tps), 30K 230s cold storm. Snapshots collected. Next: 2×131K.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
**F4 KV-cache memory accounting complete (2026-08-04).**

## Measurement method
- KV cache: llama-server startup logs (`llama_kv_cache: size = ...`) per config — the authoritative source. Values captured during F2/F3 run windows (no extra restarts).
- Model: llama-server `load_tensors: ROCm0 model buffer size`.
- System memory: `free` + rocm-smi snapshots during runs.
- **Caveat:** rocm-smi VRAM reports only ~197-203 MB on the Strix Halo iGPU — that's the small dedicated carve-out, NOT the unified LPDDR5X footprint. The real footprint is in system memory (model 24.7 GiB). Use llama-server logs + free, not rocm-smi VRAM, for accounting.

## Per-config KV cache (q8_0, 10 layers, K+V)

| Config | total_ctx | slots | KV total | KV/slot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3x43.7K (baseline) | 131072 | 3 | 1362.7 MiB | 454.2 MiB |
| 6x43.7K (hist) | 262144 | 6 | 2725.3 MiB | 454.2 MiB |
| 8x32.8K (hist) | 262144 | 8 | 2720.0 MiB | 340.0 MiB |
| 4x65.5K (cand) | 262144 | 4 | 2720.0 MiB | 680.0 MiB |
| 3x87.4K (cand) | 262144 | 3 | 2725.3 MiB | 908.4 MiB |
| 2x131K (cand) | 262144 | 2 | 2720.0 MiB | 1360.0 MiB |

**Key finding: total KV memory depends on TOTAL context (ctx_size × layers × 2 bytes q8_0), NOT slot count.** All 262144-ctx configs = ~2.72 GiB KV regardless of slot split. Slot count only redistributes KV per slot (smaller per-slot ctx = smaller per-slot KV).

## Headroom table (model 24.7 GiB + KV)

| Config | Model+KV | Headroom vs 87 GiB avail |
|---|---|---|
| 3x43.7K | 25.96 GiB | 61.0 GiB |
| all 262144-ctx | 27.29 GiB | 59.7 GiB |

## ~71GB claim verdict
**CONFIRMED (conservatively).** System: 124 GiB total, ~87 GiB measured available. Largest config (262144 ctx): model 24.7 GiB + KV 2.7 GiB = 27.3 GiB → ~60 GiB headroom. The intake's '~71GB available' is validated; even doubling ctx to 262144 barely moves total memory (KV +1.36 GiB vs baseline). Memory is NOT a constraint for any candidate config — compute/prefill latency is (see F3 findings).

F4 ACs 1-4 met. Full findings posted to parent.

data.comment:
**F5 session-retention projection complete (2026-08-04).**

Script: `proxy/benchmarks/project_session_retention.py` (committed with F5 branch; 8 tests). Data: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-08-03/daytime_sessions.csv` (433 sessions, 186 with max_context; peak concurrency 21). Nighttime CSV is empty (usage-report skill only emits daytime).

## Per-config full-local session share (day schedule)

| Config | slots | clamp | context-only full-local | concurrency-aware expected | raised-cap (12.3K→clamp) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline 3x43.7K | 3 | 39594 | 40/186 (21.5%) | 5.7 (3.1%) | 96 (51.6%) |
| 4x65.5K | 4 | 61440 | 54/186 (29.0%) | 10.3 (5.5%) | 138 (74.2%) |
| 3x87.4K | 3 | 83285 | 59/186 (31.7%) | 8.4 (4.5%) | 153 (82.3%) |
| 2x131K | 2 | 126976 | 62/186 (33.3%) | 5.9 (3.2%) | 165 (88.7%) |

## Key findings

1. **Concurrency dominates over context**: with peak 21 concurrent sessions vs 2-4 slots, expected full-local retention is 3-5.5% regardless of config. Larger context (2x131K admits 33.3% context-only) is cancelled by fewer slots (2) → worst concurrency-aware share (3.2%). **4x65.5K (4 slots) maximizes concurrency-aware retention (5.5%)** despite admitting fewer contexts.
2. **Raising the persistence cap (session_slot_max_prompt_tokens 12288 → clamp) is the bigger lever**: 51.6%→88.7% full-local context-only share; 154 sessions (2x131K) become full-local. But concurrency still caps realized retention.
3. **Context-only shares confirm the F3 finding**: larger per-slot ctx admits more sessions (21.5%→33.3%), but the marginal gain (12pp) is small vs. the concurrency penalty (fewer slots).
4. Night data unavailable (empty CSV) — day-only projection; methodology documented in script docstring.

ACs 1-4 met. Session-ID list for raised-cap variant in script output (154 IDs for 2x131K).

Resolved as part of LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C. Root cause was twofold:

Rewrote the test to patch metrics._enabled=False instead of reloading the module, exercising the same degraded-path contract without corrupting shared module state.

Proxy logs confirm: `[local] POST .../chat/completions ... session={'x-client-request-id': ..., 'x-session-affinity': '019fdb4f-...'}`. So the 'multiple agents starting up' scenario in this item is **explicit sessions** — the adaptive lease (LP-0MRDUQ9QC003LDDP) already applies to them (`_try_acquire_local_dispatch` gated by `session_id and session_explicit`, router.py:717).

3. **The remaining gap is the explicit-session adaptive lease sufficiency.** Formula: base 60s + est_tokens x 0.015s/token, cap 1500s (`_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds`, router_helpers.py:576). For a 60K-token prompt the lease is ~960s; but very large contexts (>96K est tokens) hit the 1500s cap, and 0.015s/token may under-estimate prefill on slow hardware. Log evidence (2026-08-07 09:20-09:26Z): session 019fdb4f held the lease while 019fdb51/019fdb53 were repeatedly `local_dispatch_denied` — the gate works while the lease holds; the failure mode is lease expiry mid-prefill, after which a competing agent's request would be admitted.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
**Nuance added (operator Q&A 2026-08-04): long tool-call gaps (agent subprocesses running minutes).**

The binding constraint for a session waiting on a long tool call is NOT the dispatch lease (60s) — it is:
1. **slot idle timeout 3s** (`session_slot_timeout_seconds`): the session's KV slot is released after 3s idle in llama-server.
2. **KV save cap 12.3K** (`session_slot_max_prompt_tokens`): save/restore is skipped above 12.3K estimated tokens, so the session's context is NOT persisted — a returning session re-prefills the full history (163s for 27K under contention, measured).

So raising the dispatch lease alone would be counterproductive: it would block other sessions for the tool-call duration WITHOUT preserving the returning session's KV (worst of both worlds).

**Recommendation additions:**
- Raise `session_slot_max_prompt_tokens` to the per-slot clamp (F6 lever) so KV saves cover real agent contexts; requires the adaptive save timeout (`session_slot_timeout_per_token_seconds`) and watchdog guards (LP-0MS91DHPZ001VWQO) to avoid GPU wedging on large-context serialization.
- Scale `session_slot_timeout_seconds` with the dispatch lease for explicit sessions: an active agentic session mid tool-call should hold its slot warm for the tool-call duration (not 3s), so the returning request restores KV instead of re-prefilling.
- These are orthogonal to the anonymous-lease fix (LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI); both belong in the follow-up scope.

## Plan: Adaptive dispatch lease for anonymous/non-explicit sessions

**Approach decision:** Apply the adaptive lease timeout (base 60 + est_tokens x per_token_seconds, cap 1500) to anonymous sessions via `_increment_local_active_queries` (the path anonymous requests actually take), passing `body_json`. Chosen over the n_past-based refresh alternative because AC1 requires ">= base + est_tokens x per_token_seconds, capped, verified hermetically" — the exact adaptive formula — and it reuses the existing helper from LP-0MRDUQ9QC003LDDP with minimal change. Base 60s lease unchanged (AC3, LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P rationale).

### Child features (test-first ordering)

1. **Hermetic tests: anonymous-session adaptive lease** (LP-0MSIC2OC40071CRR) — hermetic tests asserting adaptive lease duration for large anonymous prompts, base 60s for small prompts, and no orphan_cleanup of active prefills across repeated cleanup-loop runs.
2. **Implement adaptive lease for anonymous sessions** (LP-0MSIC2UJX007C0IR) — extend `_increment_local_active_queries` (router_helpers.py:676) with optional `body_json`; pass `body_json` at router.py:769; keep base 60s and non-explicit immediate record removal.
3. **Verify full suite and repeated-run stability** (LP-0MSIC2ZX0007UTEK) — full proxy suite green; >=5 repeated hermetic runs with no orphan_cleanup of active prefills; no dispatch-lease regressions.

Dependencies: 2→1, 3→2 (tests before implementation before verification).

### Key files
- proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:676 (`_increment_local_active_queries`) and 576 (`_get_adaptive_lease_timeout_seconds`)
- proxy/proxy/router.py:717 (gating), 769 (anonymous call site)
- proxy/tests/test_abandoned_future.py (adaptive lease tests), proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py

### Plan: changelog
- 2026-08-07: Created 3 child features, added dependency edges, ran 6 automated review stages (all passed; no changes required).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Which of the two suggested approaches (adaptive timeout for non-explicit sessions, or n_past-based expires_at refresh) should the fix use?" Answer (plan, from parent AC1): Adaptive timeout applied via `_increment_local_active_queries` — AC1 explicitly requires the lease to be ">= base + est_tokens x per_token_seconds, capped", which is the adaptive formula. The n_past refresh is documented as an alternative but not selected. Evidence: LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI description (Suggested approach), LP-0MRDUQ9QC003LDDP (completed adaptive lease for explicit sessions).
- Q: "Should the base lease timeout be raised?" Answer (plan, from parent AC3 + related LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P): No — base stays 60s; only the anonymous-session initial lease becomes adaptive. Evidence: LP-0MSEHMMBK0062ZPI AC3, LP-0MRHV4UYE0013F6P (180s->60s reduction rationale).
- Q: "Should the anonymous-session dispatch record removal on completion change?" Answer (plan, from router.py:443-460 comment): No — non-explicit sessions still get their record removed immediately on completion; only the in-flight (active) lease duration changes. Evidence: proxy/proxy/router.py:443-460.
- OPEN QUESTION (producer): Should the streaming-refresh gate at router.py:1185 (`session_id and session_explicit`) also be extended to anonymous sessions for very long streams? The current plan covers the prefill-phase lease (AC1/AC2 focus); a long anonymous *streaming* request that outlives the adaptive lease could still hit mid-stream cleanup. Not in the current ACs; if in scope, add as a follow-up child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (Plan for LP-0MSF1PUM90099ZSW)

- Q1: "Tool-call-only stalls — re-route or terminate?" Answer (operator): "b" — Terminate with the enriched error; no re-route. Final: tool-call-only stalls terminate; re-route is reserved for reasoning-only stalls (zero tool_calls, zero final content).
- Q2: "Partial final-answer content — only re-route when zero content committed, re-route anyway, or buffer until commit point?" Answer (operator): "c - log these events as warnings" — Buffer output until a commit point; re-route discards the buffer; re-route events logged as warnings. Final: buffering approach (option c), with warning logging.
- Q3: "Implementation approach — pre-consume/buffer in fallback chain vs typed exception?" Answer (operator): "your call". Final (plan): extended pre-flight buffering in provider.py (option a), reusing `_preflight_streaming_response`; finer chunk classification distinguishes final content vs tool_calls vs reasoning; `_handle_remote_streaming` stall behavior unchanged (yields error event; pre-flight consumer decides).
- Q4: "Commit-point definition — first final-answer content chunk?" Answer (operator): "a" — Accept strict first-content commit, with a tick-tock "thinking…" keepalive to the client during long buffered phases. Final: commit = first final-answer content chunk; keepalive sent during buffering.
- Q5: "Client-visible marker — SSE comment, log-only, or both?" Answer (operator): "a" — Yes, emit SSE comment `: re-route provider=a->b reason=stall_after_reasoning` on re-route. Final: SSE comment on re-route.
- Q6: "Idle-timeout — analysis task first, keep 120s, or raise to 240 directly?" Answer (operator): "raise to 240 initially then do a) to refine". Final: F4 raises to 240s initially (with documented tradeoff); F5 computes the stall-gap distribution and refines the value; F5 depends on F4.

### Research notes

- Reviewed current implementation: `_delta_has_content` (proxy_remote.py:558) counts content/tool_calls/reasoning_content as content-bearing (LP-0MS8XAPXT009W3CL); `_terminate_after_content` (proxy_remote.py:1157/1221/1284) terminates after-content stalls without re-route (LP-0MS9FR9LG002AJ4C). `_preflight_streaming_response` (provider.py:1697) pre-consumes to first content-bearing chunk and raises `StreamingPreContentError` (LP-0MSETOTWY000SU0Z) — the mechanism this plan extends.
- Stall evidence: 60 stall detections in current log window; 37/37 client-visible errors are `stall_after_content` on opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash; ~31% stall rate on that provider; session recordings show large reasoning_content volumes with zero final content in most failing sessions.
- Idle timeout currently 120s (config.yaml:562); opencode-go pauses >120s mid-generation while alive; raising to 240s reduces false stalls but slows true-failure detection.

Referenced paths verified accurate: proxy/proxy/provider.py (threshold functions and call site) and proxy/config.yaml (lines 392, 401). No child items exist. No changes.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies** — No child items → no-op. ACs are ordered test-first (AC1/AC2 unit tests, AC4 regression, AC3 operational evidence). discovered-from item LP-0MS9GAN2P009KK6G is completed/in_review — not blocking. No changes.
4. **Scope sizing** — No child items → no-op. Effort Small (expected 6.08h) — a deliverable increment. No changes.
5. **Acceptance & testability** — All 4 ACs are pass/fail and testable. AC3's physical_slot_cap (43776) is defined in the description. No changes.
6. **Polish & handoff** — Description is clear, well-formatted, actionable. No changes.

## Implementation notes (verified against code)

- Root cause confirmed: _effective_large_context_thresholds (provider.py:538) clamps BOTH cold and warm to cap = ctx//slots − 4096 = 39594 (131072//3 − 4096); _should_skip_local (provider.py:728) Check 2 (new_tokens = estimated × (1 − cached_ratio) > cold) is unreachable when cold == warm, because Check 1 fires for every estimate above the cap and the estimated ≤ cold short-circuit catches everything below.
- The fix requires BOTH a code change (clamp only WARM to the per-slot cap; keep COLD as the economic new-token threshold) AND a config change: cold=60000 > clamped warm=39594 would leave Check 2 unreachable, so cold must be lowered below the effective warm (AC1 requires cold < warm for the production config).
- Existing LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 regression tests (proxy/tests/test_provider_per_slot_ctx.py) constrain the WARM threshold only (test_ctx_size_8_slots_clamps_warm_to_per_slot, test_ctx_size_6_slots_clamps_higher, test_skips_oversized_prompt_that_previously_truncated), so they remain green with the fix — supporting AC4.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION** (directed to: implementer / operator; matters because it sets routing economics): What exact cold threshold value should the production config use? The suggested approach proposes cold ≈ 30k new-token threshold with warm = per-slot cap (39594). Options: (a) cold=30000 as suggested; (b) keep cold=60000 — NOT viable, since warm is bounded by physical slot capacity and cold must be < warm for Check 2 to be reachable; (c) some other value in (0, 39594). Any value with cold < effective warm satisfies AC1; the choice only affects how much new (uncached) prefill is acceptable locally. Evidence: work item description "Suggested approach" section; effort_and_risk unknowns (LP-C0MSI4ANXF003RBR5).

Implementation complete.

## Changes
- **proxy/proxy/handlers.py**: Added _resolve_client_ip(request) helper returning (ip, source). get_llama_local_status now accepts request: Request (FastAPI injects it) and logs client_ip + client_ip_source in the status_request extra dict.
- **proxy/proxy/utils.py**: Added KeyValueFormatter — renders structured extra fields as inline key=value pairs in the plain-text log (the stock Formatter silently drops extra). Wired into both file and console handlers in setup_logging(). Booleans render lowercase (true/false), None as None, non-scalars JSON-encoded.
- **proxy/tests/test_status_logging.py**: 13 new tests — client IP resolution (direct, XFF, X-Real-IP, chain-first, precedence, unknown), ASGI endpoint logging (direct + XFF header), all-fields-present, and KeyValueFormatter rendering.

## IP precedence decision (AC1 adjustment)
Spec text reads client.host-first with header fallback, but the '(reverse-proxy safe)' requirement demands header preference when present — otherwise a reverse proxy's address is logged and pollers are not attributable. Implemented: X-Forwarded-For (first entry) -> X-Real-IP -> request.client.host, with source noted (header vs direct) in every line. Audit Phase 2 endorsed this as an intentional, documented adjustment.

## Verification
- Full suite from worktree: 1896 passed (1883 at HEAD + 13 new), 6 skipped. ruff clean on changed files.
- AC4 harness: exercised the real production code path (FastAPI router -> handler -> logger extra -> KeyValueFormatter -> TimedRotatingFileHandler -> proxy.log) via ASGI; grep of the written log shows: 'status_request active_query=false available_slots=0 client_ip=127.0.0.1 client_ip_source=direct ...' and 'client_ip=192.168.0.191 client_ip_source=header ...'.
- AC4 note: the live /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log still shows bare status_request lines because the deployed proxy (systemd/uvicorn from main checkout) runs pre-change code. The payload appears in the live log once this change is deployed (release process). Not restarting the production proxy during implementation.
- Audit verdict: AC2/AC3/AC5 met, AC1 adjusted, AC4 unmet (deployment-dependent; harness-verified).

data.comment:
## Lease scaling analysis (2026-08-08 audit burst, 15:55-16:10)

The dispatch lease IS scaled with prompt size, but only for the in-flight request. Formula: min(base 60s + raw_est_tokens x 0.015, 1500s). Raw estimate is the chars/4 heuristic WITHOUT the 1.69 routing multiplier.

Observed adaptive lease values per audit session (est tokens = routing estimate / 1.69):

| Session | Local turns | Est tokens | Adaptive lease | Max prefill | Max turn |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 019fe1e2 | 45 | 1.2k-14.7k | 77-280s | 69s | 74s |
| 019fe1e5 | 41 | 1.3k-19.2k | 79-348s | 62s | 124s |
| 019fe1e6 | 26 | 1.2k-12.5k | 78-247s | 102s | 117s |
| 019fe1e7 | 17 | 1.4k-19.8k | 81-356s | 65s | 74s |

19 local turns had prefill (incl. llama-server queue wait) > 60s; the adaptive lease covered these where base 60s would not. The 273k-token session hits the 1500s cap.

Key finding for this change: the scaling does NOT extend the cross-session blocking window. At stream finish the lease resets to the base 60s (never adaptive), and during decode it is refreshed on every data chunk. All 198 denies came from fixed 60s cooldown ghosts. Reducing base to 15s shrinks both the cooldown and the acquisition lease only marginally (32k-token prompt: 540s -> 495s), preserving prefill protection.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation complete. Added `_recover_stuck_global_active_queries` (proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py) mirroring the existing local-counter recovery, wired into `_dispatch_cleanup_loop` (proxy/proxy/server.py) to run every 10s in-process (no restart required).

**Detection heuristic:** the global `active_queries` counter is only incremented on the main routing path (router.py), which always increments `local_active_queries` too (via `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` for explicit sessions or `_increment_local_active_queries` for anonymous ones); remote concurrency-limit fallback never touches it. So `active_queries > 0` with `local_active_queries == 0` and no active dispatch records proves the counter leaked. Recovery resets to 0 and logs WARNING with the previous value.

**Decision (documented):** no time-based threshold was added — the no-active-work heuristic is already strong evidence of stuck-ness, and ACs do not require timing state. Lock acquisitions are strictly sequential (no nesting), matching existing patterns.

**Tests (6 new, all green; full suite 1881 passed):**
- test_local_dispatch_gate.py: stuck counter reset / no-op with active streams / no-op with local queries in flight / no-op at 0 / legacy mode
- test_llama_local_status.py: end-to-end status endpoint reports active_query=true when stuck, false after in-process recovery (AC3)

**Observation (non-blocking):** `per_model_queries` counters can leak the same way, but they are not read by the status endpoint nor used for gating — no user-visible impact; possible future follow-up.

Implemented and pushed to dev as commit 19d8089.

## Changes
**proxy/proxy/provider.py**
- Added `_usage_limit_account_key()`: usage-limit quarantine now keys on the API-key ACCOUNT (`api_key_env@endpoint`), not the endpoint alone. Entries with different `api_key_env` on the same gateway (opencode-go vs opencode-go-2) are treated as independent limits.
- `resolve_provider` / `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`: usage-limit reset checks and same-request exclusions use the account key; endpoint-based failure-domain grouping for hard failures (stall/5xx) is unchanged (LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F).
- Both fallback cycles (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`): GoUsageLimitError/FreeUsageLimitError-with-reset-time quarantines only the failing account; same-request exclusion adds the account key so a sibling account is still attempted.

**proxy/tests/test_usage_limit_reset.py**
- Reworked `test_remote_fallback_usage_limit_reset_quarantines_account_not_gateway` (was `..._blocks_same_domain`): asserts the different-account sibling IS contacted and only the failing account is quarantined.
- Added `test_remote_fallback_usage_limit_reset_blocks_shared_account`: entries sharing an `api_key_env` are still quarantined together.
- Updated daily-variant, expiry/resume, resolve_provider, and proxy_with_fallback tests to account-key semantics.

## Tests
- Full proxy pytest suite: 2014 passed, 6 skipped (opt-in live/E2E), 0 failures.
- ruff: all checks passed.

Overnight headroom data: (1) warm threshold already scales with ctx — cheap hours log warm_threshold=100000 vs fast 39594 (auto-clamp, provider.py _effective_large_context_thresholds); cold stays 30000 in both modes. (2) Cheap-window Aug 12-13: 476 context_too_large + 215 large_context_bypass routing skips; 101 of the 215 had new_tokens in (30K,60K] (~50/night recapturable for local at cold=60K). Net: ~30/night net local gain, queue overflow roughly doubles in absolute terms (still tens/night). Conclusion: proceed with mode-aware change (cheap 60K, fast 38K) under the child validation guardrails; a single global value is NOT safe (would collapse the fast-mode band, LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). | 4 | The change does not break existing endpoints (models, completions, chat) and existing tests continue to pass | met | 359 of 365 tests pass; 6 failures in `test_metrics.py` are pre-existing `prometheus_client` issues unrelated to embeddings work |

| 3 | The doc references parent work item LP-0MN557XBD0H8B8PC | met | `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md:197` |

No other children.

# Audit: Slot registry leak: _cleanup_stale_local_dispatch never frees _slot_owners entries (LP-0MSB0RP7F000U0WJ)

Ready to close: Yes

Model: manual (no provider)

## Summary

The periodic dispatch cleanup loop `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` released expired sessions (idle_timeout and orphan_cleanup) without calling `_free_slot_assignment`, leaving permanent ghost entries in the module-level `_slot_owners` dict. Since slots are assigned lowest-free-first, the pool eventually filled with ghosts and every new session received `slot=none`, silently disabling proxy-level slot save/restore. The fix adds `_free_slot_assignment(sid)` calls in both release branches of the cleanup loop, matching the existing release paths (`_release_dispatch_lease`, `_invalidate_session_and_slot`). A new unit test verifies released sessions' slots are freed and reusable by fresh sessions, including through the production `_build_slot_context` entry point. Commit c737527 is on dev and pushed. Full proxy test suite: 1730 passed, 6 skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` frees slot registry entries for sessions it releases (idle_timeout AND orphan_cleanup branches) | met | proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:916-919 (idle_timeout branch) and :934-937 (orphan_cleanup branch) both call `_free_slot_assignment(sid)` inside the try/except pattern used by the existing release paths (router_helpers.py:786-787 in `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`, :873-874 in `_release_dispatch_lease`, session.py:871 in `_invalidate_session_and_slot`). Fix present on dev at HEAD. |
| 2 | Unit test: after an idle_timeout/orphan_cleanup release, the released session's slot is available for a new session | met | proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py:594-708 `test_cleanup_stale_frees_slot_registry_entries`: seeds expired inactive (idle_timeout) and expired active (orphan_cleanup) records plus a still-valid lease; asserts both expired records removed, their slots freed from `_slot_owners`, a fresh session reuses one of the freed slots, and the still-valid session's slot is preserved. Test passes; full test_local_dispatch_gate.py suite 31/31 passes. |
| 3 | Live verification: after churn, a fresh session receives `slot=N` (not `slot=none`) and `slot_save success` lines appear for it | adjusted | The core guarantee (fresh session receives slot=N, not none, after churn) is verified via the production entry point `_build_slot_context` in the unit test (test_local_dispatch_gate.py:690-708: `slot_id is not None` and `filename is not None` after simulated churn). The live `slot_save success` log-line confirmation was not performed — it requires a running proxy/llama-server and is environment-dependent. Adaptation documented in work-item comment. |

## Variance Decisions

|---|--------|-----------|---------------|
| 1 | LP-0MSB0RP7F000U0WJ | Live verification: after churn, a fresh session receives `slot=N` (not `slot=none`) and `slot_save success` lines appear for it | Live log verification replaced with a production-entry-point unit test (`_build_slot_context`) that verifies the root-cause behavior (fresh session gets a slot after churn). Actual `slot_save success` log lines require a running proxy/llama-server; verification was deferred to live environment. |

## Summary

The bounded cold-start scan fallback (F3 of the /admin/sessions disk-thrash fix) is implemented, tested, and verified against the live recordings tree. `COLD_SCAN_DIR_LIMIT` (default 50, configurable via `session_recording.cold_scan_dir_limit` in config.yaml) bounds the cold-scan to the N most-recent session dirs by mtime; a new `_extract_session_preview_bounded` derives `last_activity` from filename timestamps and reads at most 2 recording files per dir (earliest request for preview, earliest response for response_time/model/provider). Live measurement on the 135 GB / 9,782-dir tree: cold scan 0.277s (< 2s AC3), index capped at exactly 50 entries (AC1), warm call 0.0000s with index hit (AC4), fallback triggered only once when cold (AC5). Full proxy suite passes (2148 passed, 6 skipped). One documented variance: AC2 states "at most 1 recording file per dir"; the implementation reads at most 2 (request + response) — a bounded constant regardless of dir size, satisfying the anti-disk-thrash intent (documented in commit 338088a and the method docstring).

## Acceptance Criteria Status

| # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Cold scan visits only the N most-recent session dirs (by dir mtime; N=50 default, configurable) — never the full tree | met | `proxy/proxy/session_recorder.py:60-65` (`COLD_SCAN_DIR_LIMIT = 50`), `:109-111` (constructor param), `:148-157` (`from_config`), `:300-315` (`_rebuild_index_from_scan` sorts dirs by `d.stat().st_mtime` reverse and slices `dirs[:self.cold_scan_dir_limit]`). Live run on 9,782-dir tree: `index_size` = exactly 50. Tests: `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_configurable`, `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_default`, `test_cold_scan_dir_limit_from_config`, `test_empty_index_falls_back_to_bounded_scan` (proxy/tests/test_session_recorder.py:883-997). |
| 2 | Reads at most 1 recording file per dir (for model/provider/preview); last_activity derived from filename timestamp | adjusted | `_extract_session_preview_bounded` (session_recorder.py:324-408) reads at most **2** files per dir (earliest `-request.json` for preview_text, earliest `-response.json` for response_time/model/provider), not the stated 1 — empirically confirmed (4 reads / 2 dirs with both file types). `last_activity` derived from the newest filename timestamp via `_FILENAME_TS_RE` (`:339-344`, `:352-358`), no content read. Variance is deliberate and documented in commit 338088a ("reads at most 2 files per dir") and the method docstring; per-dir reads stay a small constant regardless of dir size (a dir may hold hundreds of files / multi-GB), fully satisfying the AC's anti-disk-thrash intent. Tests: `test_cold_scan_reads_at_most_one_file_per_dir`, `test_cold_scan_last_activity_from_filename_timestamp`. |
| 3 | Cold scan completes in < 2s on the live tree | met | Live measurement: cold `list_sessions()` against `proxy/session-recordings/` (135 GB, 9,782 dirs) completed in **0.277s** (index_size 50). Scan is structurally bounded to 50 dirs × ≤2 file reads; base-dir iteration is metadata-only (stat per entry, no content reads). |
| 4 | Rebuild populates the index so subsequent calls are warm (zero reads) | met | `_ensure_index_warm` (session_recorder.py:268-287) adds the path to `_INDEX_WARM_PATHS` after rebuild; second `list_sessions()` measured **0.0000s** with `index_hits` incremented. Default threshold is _STALL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600 s (10 min, line 209), configurable via AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT env var (AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT_ENV line 198). Tests TestStallAbort::test_stalled_call_aborts_well_before_full_budget and test_stall_abort_sets_timeout_marker pass (verified by running them; elapsed ~1s with AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT=1 vs 1800s budget). FILE SCOPE NOTE: the manifest's only changed file proxy/grandfathering-state.json is a proxy model-binding state JSON with no code; the criterion's target (_call_pi) lives in the work-item-named key file SorraAgents/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, which was read for verification. |
| 2 | **(AC2) Clean abort.** The stalled call is killed via `proc.kill()` + `proc.wait()`, a `_timeout` marker is set on the verdict, and the existing `partial — manual review required` path is followed (no fabricated verdicts). | met | Clean abort path verified in _call_pi (audit_runner.py lines ~2114-2139): on subprocess.TimeoutExpired the code calls process.kill() then process.communicate() (which waits for process exit / drains pipes — equivalent to proc.wait()), then distinguishes stall vs budget expiry via stalled = exc.timeout == stall_timeout and returns a verdict dict that sets "_timeout": True alongside "verdict": "unmet" and evidence 'Pi model call stalled (no output for {stall_timeout}s); aborted early. Manual audit required.' (or the budget-timeout variant 'timed out after {effective_timeout}s. Manual audit required.'). The evidence follows the existing manual-review pattern (no fabricated verdicts — always the honest 'unmet' with truthful stall/timed-out evidence and the _timeout marker). Note: the criterion text says 'the existing partial — manual review required path', but the actual pre-existing path (visible in the same diff, original code) returns verdict 'unmet' with 'Manual audit required.' evidence, not 'partial'; the implementation follows the actual established pattern, so the substance of the requirement is satisfied. EOF is handled by removing the fd from the dict (comment: 'select keeps reporting EOF'd fds as readable, so we must drop it to avoid a busy loop'); process exit is race-safe via process.poll() break; remaining buffered output is drained after exit. Mocked processes without real fileno (unit tests) fall back to the historical blocking process.communicate(timeout=effective_timeout), preserving the existing contract. Tests TestStallAbort use a _StallingProcess with real os.pipe() fds to exercise the select path and pass. |
| 4 | **(AC2) Configurable threshold.** `AUDIT_STALL_TIMEOUT` env var (integer, seconds); invalid values ignored with a warning. Test test_stall_timeout_env_resolution verifies all three branches (valid '120' -> 120, unset -> 600, invalid 'abc' -> 600 with 'invalid' warning written to stderr) — PASSED. |
| 5 | **(AC2) No regression on Phase-2 bash tool calls.** Phase 2 calls that legitimately go quiet during a long bash tool execution (e.g. test run) are not falsely aborted. Mitigation: the default 10 min is generous vs healthy Phase 1 (30–190 s), and the stall detection measures *subprocess output activity* (stdout bytes from the pi JSON stream). | met | No-regression mitigation verified: stall detection measures subprocess output activity on both stdout and stderr fds (select loop in _communicate_with_stall, audit_runner.py lines 1973-2003), and the default _STALL_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT = 600 s is generous vs healthy Phase 1 durations (30-190 s per the commit message and code docstring at lines 204-210), so healthy calls that emit the pi JSON stream promptly are never falsely aborted. | # | Criterion | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|-----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | **(AC3) Slot-aware dynamic ceiling.** Before launching child calls (Phase-1 AC-review and Phase-2 deep-analysis), the runner queries the proxy status endpoint ($/llama/local/status$) for `available_slots` / `total_slots`. The dynamic child-call ceiling is derived from the available headroom: `min(available_headroom, configured_max)` where `configured_max` defaults to the existing `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` value. | partial | Deep analysis timed out — manual review required. |
| 2 | **(AC3) Fail-open fallback.** When the slot query fails (timeout, HTTP error, unreachable endpoint), the runner degrades gracefully to the configured static ceiling (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`). The dynamic ceiling must never block or fail the audit when the query is unavailable. | partial | Deep analysis timed out — manual review required. |
| 3 | **(AC3) Configurable max + default.** New env var `AUDIT_MAX_CHILD_CONCURRENCY` (or reuse `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` as the max cap) with default equal to existing `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` default (2). Both static and dynamic values capped by this max. | partial | Deep analysis timed out — manual review required. |
| 4 | **(AC3) Short timeout on status query.** The proxy status endpoint query uses a short timeout (1 s, fail-open). | partial | Deep analysis timed out — manual review required. |
| 5 | **(AC3) No oscillation.** Dynamic ceiling is queried once per child-call batch dispatch (not per-call) to avoid oscillation. | partial | Deep analysis timed out — manual review required. |
